at-aigen-gottschelle.name: Ried Gottschelle
at-aigen-gottschelle.summary: The Gottschelle lies below Göttweig abbey on the south bank of the Danube, giving ripe, peppery Grüner Veltliner; Stift Göttweig's estate bottles it.
at-aigen-gottschelle.terroir: Loess over gravel and crystalline rock. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Aigen (municipality Furth bei Göttweig), with about 10 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Obere Point.

at-aigen-gottschelle-obere-point.name: Ried Gottschelle Obere Point
at-aigen-gottschelle-obere-point.summary: Obere Point is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Gottschelle at Aigen, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Gottschelle lies below Göttweig abbey on the south bank of the Danube, giving ripe, peppery Grüner Veltliner; Stift Göttweig's estate bottles it.
at-aigen-gottschelle-obere-point.terroir: Loess over gravel and crystalline rock.
at-aigen-gottschelle-obere-point.nerd_note: See the Ried Gottschelle profile for the site's history and growers.
at-aigen-gottschelle-obere-point.classification: ÖTW Erste Lage (1ÖTW) (as part of the Ried Gottschelle)

at-angern-frauengrund.name: Ried Frauengrund
at-angern-frauengrund.summary: A Ried shared by Angern and Thallern in the Krems municipality, giving supple Grüner Veltliner.
at-angern-frauengrund.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-angern-frauengrund.terroir: Loess and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Angern (municipality Krems an der Donau), with about 50 ha delimited.

at-baumgarten-bischofpoint.name: Ried Bischofpoint
at-baumgarten-bischofpoint.summary: A Mautern Ried whose name recalls episcopal ownership; Bavarian bishoprics and abbeys such as Passau, Freising and Tegernsee held much of the Wachau's vineyard land in the Middle Ages.
at-baumgarten-bischofpoint.terroir: Loess and gneiss. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Baumgarten (municipality Mautern an der Donau), with about 20 ha delimited.

at-breitenbrunn-am-neusiedler-see-kirchb.name: Ried Kirchberg
at-breitenbrunn-am-neusiedler-see-kirchb.summary: A Breitenbrunn Ried on the Leitha slopes giving structured Blaufränkisch.
at-breitenbrunn-am-neusiedler-see-kirchb.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-breitenbrunn-am-neusiedler-see-kirchb.terroir: Limestone and schist. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Breitenbrunn am Neusiedler See, with about 20 ha delimited.

at-breitenbrunn-am-neusiedler-see-sandgr.name: Ried Sandgraben
at-breitenbrunn-am-neusiedler-see-sandgr.summary: A Breitenbrunn Ried on sandy soils near the lake, giving fresh reds and whites.
at-breitenbrunn-am-neusiedler-see-sandgr.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-breitenbrunn-am-neusiedler-see-sandgr.terroir: Sand and gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Breitenbrunn am Neusiedler See, with about 60 ha delimited.

at-breitenbrunn-am-neusiedler-see-thenau.name: Ried Thenau
at-breitenbrunn-am-neusiedler-see-thenau.summary: The Breitenbrunn part of the Thenau, giving supple reds and whites near the lake.
at-breitenbrunn-am-neusiedler-see-thenau.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-breitenbrunn-am-neusiedler-see-thenau.terroir: Loam and gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Breitenbrunn am Neusiedler See, with about 70 ha delimited.

at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-ratschen.name: Ried Ratschen
at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-ratschen.summary: A Deutsch Schützen Ried on the Eisenberg giving fresh, spicy Blaufränkisch, for example from Stubits and Wachter-Wiesler.
at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-ratschen.nerd_note: Eisenberg DAC (since 2010) covers Blaufränkisch from the green schist and iron-rich loam of southern Burgenland.
at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-ratschen.terroir: Schist and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Deutsch Schützen-Eisenberg, with about 50 ha delimited.

at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-reihburg.name: Ried Reihburg
at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-reihburg.summary: The Reihburg is a small Eisenberg Ried where Uwe Schiefer makes a fine, perfumed Blaufränkisch.
at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-reihburg.nerd_note: Eisenberg DAC (since 2010) covers Blaufränkisch from the green schist and iron-rich loam of southern Burgenland.
at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-reihburg.terroir: Green schist and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Deutsch Schützen-Eisenberg, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-saybritz.name: Ried Saybritz
at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-saybritz.summary: The Saybritz is one of the top Eisenberg sites, a steep slope of green schist above Deutsch Schützen giving spicy, mineral Blaufränkisch.
at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-saybritz.terroir: Green schist and iron-rich loam, south-facing, around 300 to 360 m. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Deutsch Schützen-Eisenberg, with about 60 ha delimited.
at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-saybritz.nerd_note: The Eisenberg hill rises on the Hungarian border in southern Burgenland; Eisenberg DAC (since 2010) covers Blaufränkisch from green schist and iron-rich loam.

at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-szapary.name: Ried Szapary
at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-szapary.summary: The Szapary is named after the Hungarian noble family that once owned it. Uwe Schiefer made it famous with taut, profound Blaufränkisch from old vines, including the 'Alter Garten' parcel. Uwe Schiefer, a former Vienna sommelier, began farming the Eisenberg in the 1990s and is credited with revealing the hill's potential.
at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-szapary.terroir: Green schist and iron-rich loam high on the Eisenberg. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Deutsch Schützen-Eisenberg, with about 50 ha delimited.
at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-szapary.nerd_note: Eisenberg means 'iron hill', after the iron oxides in its soils.

at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-weinberg.name: Ried Weinberg
at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-weinberg.summary: A Deutsch Schützen Ried giving dense Blaufränkisch from iron-rich soils.
at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-weinberg.nerd_note: Eisenberg DAC (since 2010) covers Blaufränkisch from the green schist and iron-rich loam of southern Burgenland.
at-deutsch-schutzen-eisenberg-weinberg.terroir: Schist and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Deutsch Schützen-Eisenberg, with about 40 ha delimited.

at-deutschkreutz-kart.name: Ried Kart
at-deutschkreutz-kart.summary: A large Ried around Deutschkreutz, the biggest Blaufränkisch village of the district, giving supple, fruity reds; Gesellmann and others are based here.
at-deutschkreutz-kart.terroir: Loam and clay over gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Deutschkreutz, with about 510 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Baumfeld, Hollinger Weg, Kleinteucht, Kogel, Kolnhoferweg, Pallischkreuz.

at-deutschkreutz-weisses-kreuz.name: Ried Weisses Kreuz
at-deutschkreutz-weisses-kreuz.summary: A large Deutschkreutz Ried named after a wayside cross, giving fruity Blaufränkisch.
at-deutschkreutz-weisses-kreuz.nerd_note: Mittelburgenland DAC (since 2005) is dedicated to Blaufränkisch, the grape that covers about half of the district's vineyards.
at-deutschkreutz-weisses-kreuz.terroir: Loam and gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Deutschkreutz, with about 410 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Dornrainäcker, Frauenbrunnäcker, Gartenäcker, Hochacker, Hölzl, Kleinstraßäcker.

at-durnstein-hohereck.name: Ried Höhereck
at-durnstein-hohereck.summary: A high Dürnstein Ried giving fine, mineral Riesling and Grüner Veltliner, notably from Leo Alzinger.
at-durnstein-hohereck.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
at-durnstein-hohereck.terroir: Gneiss terraces at altitude. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Dürnstein, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-durnstein-hollerin.name: Ried Hollerin
at-durnstein-hollerin.summary: A small Dürnstein site giving fresh, peppery Grüner Veltliner.
at-durnstein-hollerin.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
at-durnstein-hollerin.terroir: Loess and gneiss. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Dürnstein.

at-durnstein-kaiserberg.name: Ried Kaiserberg
at-durnstein-kaiserberg.summary: A Dürnstein Ried above the town, giving firm Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-durnstein-kaiserberg.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
at-durnstein-kaiserberg.terroir: Gneiss terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Dürnstein, with about 20 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Lichtensteinerin.

at-durnstein-kaiserberg-lichtensteinerin.name: Ried Kaiserberg Lichtensteinerin
at-durnstein-kaiserberg-lichtensteinerin.summary: Lichtensteinerin is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Kaiserberg at Dürnstein, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Dürnstein Ried above the town, giving firm Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-durnstein-kaiserberg-lichtensteinerin.nerd_note: See the Ried Kaiserberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-durnstein-kellerberg.name: Ried Kellerberg
at-durnstein-kellerberg.summary: The Kellerberg is a steep, terraced slope just west of Dürnstein, and the source of some of the most powerful dry Rieslings and Grüner Veltliners of the Wachau. F.X. Pichler's Kellerberg Smaragds, with their mix of opulence, smoke and cool minerality, made the site famous in the 1990s; Knoll and Domäne Wachau also own parcels. A side valley feeds cool air into the vineyard at night, which keeps aromas fresh despite the heat of the terraces.
at-durnstein-kellerberg.terroir: About 15 ha of terraces between about 220 and 400 m, with sandy loess over primary rock of gneiss and quartz. The subrieden Wunderburg and Küss den Pfennig are named on the official map. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Dürnstein, with about 20 ha delimited.
at-durnstein-kellerberg.nerd_note: The site sits where a side valley opens behind Dürnstein; the night-time downdraught is the Kellerberg's secret, keeping very ripe wines fresh.

at-durnstein-kellerberg-kuss-den-pfennig.name: Ried Kellerberg Küss den Pfennig
at-durnstein-kellerberg-kuss-den-pfennig.summary: Küss den Pfennig is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Kellerberg at Dürnstein, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Kellerberg is a steep, terraced slope just west of Dürnstein, and the source of some of the most powerful dry Rieslings and Grüner Veltliners of the Wachau. F.X. at-durnstein-kellerberg-kuss-den-pfennig.nerd_note: See the Ried Kellerberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-durnstein-kellerberg-wunderburg.name: Ried Kellerberg Wunderburg
at-durnstein-kellerberg-wunderburg.summary: Wunderburg is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Kellerberg at Dürnstein, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Kellerberg is a steep, terraced slope just west of Dürnstein, and the source of some of the most powerful dry Rieslings and Grüner Veltliners of the Wachau. F.X. at-durnstein-liebenberg.name: Ried Liebenberg
at-durnstein-liebenberg.summary: A Dürnstein Ried giving supple, aromatic Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
at-durnstein-liebenberg.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
at-durnstein-liebenberg.terroir: Gneiss and loess on south-facing terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Dürnstein, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-durnstein-schlossberg.name: Ried Schlossberg
at-durnstein-schlossberg.summary: The slope below the ruined castle of Dürnstein, where Richard the Lionheart was held prisoner in 1192 and 1193, gives fine, mineral Riesling.
at-durnstein-schlossberg.terroir: Steep gneiss terraces under the castle rock. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Dürnstein. Named subrieden: Burgweingarten.

at-durnstein-schlossberg-burgweingarten.name: Ried Schlossberg Burgweingarten
at-durnstein-schlossberg-burgweingarten.summary: Burgweingarten is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Schlossberg at Dürnstein, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The slope below the ruined castle of Dürnstein, where Richard the Lionheart was held prisoner in 1192 and 1193, gives fine, mineral Riesling.
at-durnstein-schlossberg-burgweingarten.terroir: Steep gneiss terraces under the castle rock.
at-durnstein-schlossberg-burgweingarten.nerd_note: See the Ried Schlossberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-durnstein-schutt.name: Ried Schütt
at-durnstein-schutt.summary: The Schütt is a site of alluvial gravel and sand washed down from a side valley between Dürnstein and Loiben. Knoll's Riesling Smaragd Schütt is one of the Wachau's classics, broad and juicy with a peppery bite. Because the soils are deep and loose, vines root easily and could crop heavily, so growers keep yields small; Knoll's Schütt Rieslings are famous for ageing two decades and more.
at-durnstein-schutt.terroir: Gravel, sand and gneiss debris on a gentle fan at the foot of the hills. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Dürnstein.
at-durnstein-schutt.nerd_note: 'Schütt' means debris or rubble, describing the material the side valley dumps onto the slope.

at-egelsee-steiner-goldberg.name: Ried Steiner Goldberg
at-egelsee-steiner-goldberg.summary: A Stein Ried giving fine Riesling on crystalline rock.
at-egelsee-steiner-goldberg.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-egelsee-steiner-goldberg.terroir: Gneiss terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Egelsee (municipality Krems an der Donau).

at-eisenstadt-tatschler.name: Ried Tatschler
at-eisenstadt-tatschler.summary: The Tatschler is a limestone site on the edge of Eisenstadt where Kollwentz makes a celebrated Chardonnay, rich and taut.
at-eisenstadt-tatschler.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-eisenstadt-tatschler.terroir: Leitha limestone and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Eisenstadt, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-elsarn-am-jauerling-brandstatt.name: Ried Brandstatt
at-elsarn-am-jauerling-brandstatt.summary: The Brandstatt is a high, steep Ried in the Spitzer Graben, among the coolest of the Wachau, revived by growers such as Peter Veyder-Malberg.
at-elsarn-am-jauerling-brandstatt.terroir: Gneiss terraces above 450 m. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Elsarn am Jauerling (municipality Mühldorf), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-elsarn-am-jauerling-bruck.name: Ried Bruck
at-elsarn-am-jauerling-bruck.summary: The upper part of the Bruck Ried in the Spitzer Graben, at Elsarn, giving cool, fine Riesling.
at-elsarn-am-jauerling-bruck.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
at-elsarn-am-jauerling-bruck.terroir: Gneiss terraces at altitude. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Elsarn am Jauerling (municipality Mühldorf).

at-engelmannsbrunn-hochrain.name: Ried Hochrain
at-engelmannsbrunn-hochrain.summary: An Engelmannsbrunn Ried giving fruity Grüner Veltliner.
at-engelmannsbrunn-hochrain.nerd_note: The Wagram's loess bank runs for some 30 km along the north side of the Danube; its DAC rules put Ried wines at the top of the pyramid, with Grüner Veltliner and the local Roter Veltliner as signature grapes.
at-engelmannsbrunn-hochrain.terroir: Loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Engelmannsbrunn (municipality Kirchberg am Wagram), with about 20 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Rabengassl.

at-engelmannsbrunn-hochrain-rabengassl.name: Ried Hochrain Rabengassl
at-engelmannsbrunn-hochrain-rabengassl.summary: Rabengassl is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Hochrain at Engelmannsbrunn, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. An Engelmannsbrunn Ried giving fruity Grüner Veltliner.
at-engelmannsbrunn-hochrain-rabengassl.nerd_note: See the Ried Hochrain profile for the site's history and growers.

at-fels-am-wagram-brunnthal.name: Ried Brunnthal
at-fels-am-wagram-brunnthal.summary: A Fels Ried where Leth makes fine Riesling and Grüner Veltliner on loess and gravel.
at-fels-am-wagram-brunnthal.nerd_note: The Wagram's loess bank runs for some 30 km along the north side of the Danube; its DAC rules put Ried wines at the top of the pyramid, with Grüner Veltliner and the local Roter Veltliner as signature grapes.
at-fels-am-wagram-brunnthal.terroir: Loess and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Fels am Wagram, with about 40 ha delimited.

at-fels-am-wagram-schafflerberg.name: Ried Schafflerberg
at-fels-am-wagram-schafflerberg.summary: A Wagram Ried on the loess escarpment, giving fresh Grüner Veltliner and Roter Veltliner.
at-fels-am-wagram-schafflerberg.nerd_note: The Wagram's loess bank runs for some 30 km along the north side of the Danube; its DAC rules put Ried wines at the top of the pyramid, with Grüner Veltliner and the local Roter Veltliner as signature grapes.
at-fels-am-wagram-schafflerberg.terroir: Deep loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Fels am Wagram, with about 50 ha delimited.

at-fels-am-wagram-scheiben.name: Ried Scheiben
at-fels-am-wagram-scheiben.summary: The Scheiben is one of the top Rieden of Fels am Wagram, a long terrace of deep loess where Leth makes a creamy, spicy Grüner Veltliner. The Wagram is a twenty-mile escarpment of loess that marks the ancient shore of the Danube. Franz Leth's family estate in Fels has helped show that the Wagram can produce Grüner Veltliner of real depth.
at-fels-am-wagram-scheiben.terroir: Deep loess, up to many metres thick, over gravel and marine sediments, on south-facing slopes. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Fels am Wagram, with about 90 ha delimited.
at-fels-am-wagram-scheiben.nerd_note: 'Wagram' is thought to come from 'Wogenrain', the edge of the waves: the river once ran along the foot of this bank.

at-feuersbrunn-rosenberg.name: Ried Rosenberg
at-feuersbrunn-rosenberg.summary: The Rosenberg at Feuersbrunn is the top Grüner Veltliner site of Bernhard Ott, whose deep, spicy, biodynamically farmed wines helped put the Wagram on the international map. Ott makes only Grüner Veltliner at the top of his range; the Rosenberg is his most powerful and age-worthy wine, while 'Der Ott' blends younger parcels, and he also ferments some cuvées in clay amphorae.
at-feuersbrunn-rosenberg.terroir: Loess over gravel and calcareous sediments on a south-facing slope. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Feuersbrunn (municipality Grafenwörth), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-feuersbrunn-spiegel.name: Ried Spiegel
at-feuersbrunn-spiegel.summary: A Feuersbrunn Ried where Bernhard Ott makes a fine, aromatic Grüner Veltliner.
at-feuersbrunn-spiegel.nerd_note: The Wagram's loess bank runs for some 30 km along the north side of the Danube; its DAC rules put Ried wines at the top of the pyramid, with Grüner Veltliner and the local Roter Veltliner as signature grapes.
at-feuersbrunn-spiegel.terroir: Loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Feuersbrunn (municipality Grafenwörth), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-franzhausen-gaisruck.name: Ried Gaisruck
at-franzhausen-gaisruck.summary: A Ried on the Nußdorf hills giving fresh white wines.
at-franzhausen-gaisruck.nerd_note: Traisental DAC (since 2006) covers Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from one of the smallest wine areas of Lower Austria, on the south side of the Danube.
at-franzhausen-gaisruck.terroir: Conglomerate and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Franzhausen (municipality Nußdorf ob der Traisen).

at-furth-gottschelle.name: Ried Gottschelle
at-furth-gottschelle.summary: The Gottschelle lies below Göttweig abbey on the south bank of the Danube, giving ripe, peppery Grüner Veltliner; Stift Göttweig's estate bottles it.
at-furth-gottschelle.terroir: Loess over gravel and crystalline rock. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Furth (municipality Furth bei Göttweig), with about 30 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Obere Point.

at-furth-gottschelle-obere-point.name: Ried Gottschelle Obere Point
at-furth-gottschelle-obere-point.summary: Obere Point is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Gottschelle at Furth, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Gottschelle lies below Göttweig abbey on the south bank of the Danube, giving ripe, peppery Grüner Veltliner; Stift Göttweig's estate bottles it.
at-furth-gottschelle-obere-point.terroir: Loess over gravel and crystalline rock.
at-furth-gottschelle-obere-point.nerd_note: See the Ried Gottschelle profile for the site's history and growers.
at-furth-gottschelle-obere-point.classification: ÖTW Erste Lage (1ÖTW) (as part of the Ried Gottschelle)

at-furth-leukuschberg.name: Ried Leukuschberg
at-furth-leukuschberg.summary: A Ried on the hills below Göttweig abbey, giving fresh white wines.
at-furth-leukuschberg.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-furth-leukuschberg.terroir: Loess and gneiss. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Furth (municipality Furth bei Göttweig), with about 20 ha delimited.

at-furth-oberfeld.name: Ried Oberfeld
at-furth-oberfeld.summary: A Furth Ried below Göttweig abbey, giving fruity Grüner Veltliner.
at-furth-oberfeld.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-furth-oberfeld.terroir: Loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Furth (municipality Furth bei Göttweig), with about 30 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Hintere Point.

at-furth-oberfeld-hintere-point.name: Ried Oberfeld Hintere Point
at-furth-oberfeld-hintere-point.summary: Hintere Point is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Oberfeld at Furth, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Furth Ried below Göttweig abbey, giving fruity Grüner Veltliner.

at-gedersdorf-moosburgerin.name: Ried Moosburgerin
at-gedersdorf-moosburgerin.summary: A Gedersdorf Ried associated with Mantlerhof, giving rich, spicy Grüner Veltliner on loess.
at-gedersdorf-moosburgerin.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-gedersdorf-moosburgerin.terroir: Deep loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Gedersdorf, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-gedersdorf-spiegel.name: Ried Spiegel
at-gedersdorf-spiegel.summary: A Gedersdorf Ried on loess, giving creamy Grüner Veltliner, notably from Mantlerhof.
at-gedersdorf-spiegel.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-gedersdorf-spiegel.terroir: Loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Gedersdorf. Named subrieden: Altmandl.

at-gedersdorf-spiegel-altmandl.summary: Altmandl is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Spiegel at Gedersdorf, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Gedersdorf Ried on loess, giving creamy Grüner Veltliner, notably from Mantlerhof.

at-gedersdorf-wieland.name: Ried Wieland
at-gedersdorf-wieland.summary: A small Gedersdorf Ried giving fresh white wines.

at-getzersdorf-berg.name: Ried Berg
at-getzersdorf-berg.summary: The Berg at Getzersdorf is a steep terraced slope of conglomerate where Markus Huber makes an intense, saline Riesling.
at-getzersdorf-berg.nerd_note: Traisental DAC (since 2006) covers Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from one of the smallest wine areas of Lower Austria, on the south side of the Danube.
at-getzersdorf-berg.terroir: Calcareous conglomerate terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Getzersdorf (municipality Inzersdorf-Getzersdorf), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-getzersdorf-engelreich.name: Ried Engelreich
at-getzersdorf-engelreich.summary: A Getzersdorf Ried giving finely structured Grüner Veltliner, notably from Markus Huber.
at-getzersdorf-engelreich.nerd_note: Traisental DAC (since 2006) covers Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from one of the smallest wine areas of Lower Austria, on the south side of the Danube.
at-getzersdorf-engelreich.terroir: Conglomerate and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Getzersdorf (municipality Inzersdorf-Getzersdorf), with about 20 ha delimited.

at-getzersdorf-pletzengraben.name: Ried Pletzengraben
at-getzersdorf-pletzengraben.summary: The Pletzengraben is a cool, high Ried in the hills of the Traisental, one of Austria's smallest DACs, on the south side of the Danube. Its chalky conglomerate soils give Grüner Veltliner and Riesling with a cool, salty precision.
at-getzersdorf-pletzengraben.terroir: Calcareous conglomerate and gravel at around 350 m, south-facing; the cool air of the Alpine foothills reaches the valley at night. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Getzersdorf (municipality Inzersdorf-Getzersdorf).
at-getzersdorf-pletzengraben.nerd_note: The Traisental's limestone-rich gravels, deposited by the ancient Traisen river, set it apart from the gneiss and loess of the Danube sites to the north.

at-gobelsburg-spiegel.name: Ried Spiegel
at-gobelsburg-spiegel.summary: The Spiegel is a broad loess slope near Langenlois giving creamy, peppery Grüner Veltliner, from Fred Loimer, Jurtschitsch and others.
at-gobelsburg-spiegel.terroir: Deep loess and loam on south-facing slopes. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Gobelsburg (municipality Langenlois), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-gols-altenberg.name: Ried Altenberg
at-gols-altenberg.summary: A Gols Ried on the edge of the Parndorf plateau, giving firm Blaufränkisch and Zweigelt.
at-gols-altenberg.nerd_note: Neusiedlersee DAC (since 2012) is built on Zweigelt for dry reds and on botrytised sweet wines from the lake's mists.
at-gols-altenberg.terroir: Gravel and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Gols, with about 60 ha delimited.

at-gols-gabarinza.name: Ried Gabarinza
at-gols-gabarinza.summary: The Gabarinza at Gols gives Heinrich's long-running red blend of the same name, built on Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch.
at-gols-gabarinza.nerd_note: Neusiedlersee DAC (since 2012) is built on Zweigelt for dry reds and on botrytised sweet wines from the lake's mists.
at-gols-gabarinza.terroir: Gravel and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Gols, with about 20 ha delimited.

at-gols-salzberg.name: Ried Salzberg
at-gols-salzberg.summary: The Salzberg at Gols, on the northern shore of Lake Neusiedl, is the source of Gernot and Heike Heinrich's flagship red, a Blaufränkisch-based wine that showed what the Parndorf plateau's slopes can do. The Heinrichs farm biodynamically and belong to Pannobile, a group of Gols growers who promote local varieties and site-driven blends.
at-gols-salzberg.terroir: Gravel, sand and loam on the slope down from the Parndorf plateau; warm Pannonian climate moderated by the lake. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Gols, with about 40 ha delimited.
at-gols-salzberg.nerd_note: Gols is one of Austria's largest wine villages; its growers led the red-wine boom of the 1990s.

at-gols-ungerberg.name: Ried Ungerberg
at-gols-ungerberg.summary: A Gols Ried on the slopes towards the lake, giving fruity Zweigelt and St. Laurent.
at-gols-ungerberg.nerd_note: Neusiedlersee DAC (since 2012) is built on Zweigelt for dry reds and on botrytised sweet wines from the lake's mists.
at-gols-ungerberg.terroir: Sand and gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Gols, with about 50 ha delimited.

at-gosing-bodenleiten.name: Ried Bodenleiten
at-gosing-bodenleiten.summary: A Gösing Ried giving supple Grüner Veltliner.
at-gosing-bodenleiten.nerd_note: The Wagram's loess bank runs for some 30 km along the north side of the Danube; its DAC rules put Ried wines at the top of the pyramid, with Grüner Veltliner and the local Roter Veltliner as signature grapes.
at-gosing-bodenleiten.terroir: Loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Gösing (municipality Fels am Wagram), with about 10 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Berg Eisenhut.

at-gosing-bodenleiten-berg-eisenhut.nerd_note: See the Ried Bodenleiten profile for the site's history and growers.

at-gosing-fumberg.name: Ried Fumberg
at-gosing-fumberg.summary: A Ried above Gösing on the Wagram escarpment, giving firm Grüner Veltliner.
at-gosing-fumberg.nerd_note: The Wagram's loess bank runs for some 30 km along the north side of the Danube; its DAC rules put Ried wines at the top of the pyramid, with Grüner Veltliner and the local Roter Veltliner as signature grapes.
at-gosing-fumberg.terroir: Loess and marine gravels. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Gösing (municipality Fels am Wagram), with about 40 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Welfel.

at-gosing-fumberg-welfel.summary: Welfel is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Fumberg at Gösing, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Ried above Gösing on the Wagram escarpment, giving firm Grüner Veltliner.
at-gosing-fumberg-welfel.nerd_note: See the Ried Fumberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-gosing-goldberg.nerd_note: The Wagram's loess bank runs for some 30 km along the north side of the Danube; its DAC rules put Ried wines at the top of the pyramid, with Grüner Veltliner and the local Roter Veltliner as signature grapes.
at-gosing-goldberg.terroir: Loess and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Gösing (municipality Fels am Wagram), with about 40 ha delimited.

at-gottlesbrunn-altenberg.name: Ried Altenberg
at-gottlesbrunn-altenberg.summary: A Göttlesbrunn Ried giving fruity reds and some whites.
at-gottlesbrunn-altenberg.nerd_note: Carnuntum DAC (since 2019) is built on Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch reds and on white wines from Grüner Veltliner, Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc.
at-gottlesbrunn-altenberg.terroir: Loess and loam. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Göttlesbrunn (municipality Göttlesbrunn-Arbesthal), with about 30 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Eisenbach, Zwiering.

at-gottlesbrunn-altenberg-eisenbach.summary: Eisenbach is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Altenberg at Göttlesbrunn, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Göttlesbrunn Ried giving fruity reds and some whites.

at-gottlesbrunn-haidacker.name: Ried Haidacker
at-gottlesbrunn-haidacker.summary: A Göttlesbrunn Ried giving supple Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch.
at-gottlesbrunn-haidacker.nerd_note: Carnuntum DAC (since 2019) is built on Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch reds and on white wines from Grüner Veltliner, Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc.
at-gottlesbrunn-haidacker.terroir: Loess and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Göttlesbrunn (municipality Göttlesbrunn-Arbesthal), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-gottlesbrunn-rosenberg.name: Ried Rosenberg
at-gottlesbrunn-rosenberg.summary: The Rosenberg is the best-known red-wine site of Göttlesbrunn, the heart of Carnuntum, east of Vienna. Gerhard Markowitsch and others make structured Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch here, firm and peppery, with the warmth of the Pannonian plain. Göttlesbrunn's growers turned Carnuntum from a bulk area into a red-wine name in the 1990s; 'Rubin Carnuntum' is the regional label for their Zweigelt.
at-gottlesbrunn-rosenberg.terroir: Loess and loam over gravel and limestone on a gentle south-facing slope. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Göttlesbrunn (municipality Göttlesbrunn-Arbesthal), with about 20 ha delimited.
at-gottlesbrunn-rosenberg.nerd_note: Carnuntum is named after the Roman legionary city on the Danube nearby, capital of Pannonia Superior.

at-gottlesbrunn-schuttenberg.name: Ried Schüttenberg
at-gottlesbrunn-schuttenberg.summary: A Göttlesbrunn Ried on gravel and loess, giving firm, spicy reds.
at-gottlesbrunn-schuttenberg.nerd_note: Carnuntum DAC (since 2019) is built on Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch reds and on white wines from Grüner Veltliner, Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc.
at-gottlesbrunn-schuttenberg.terroir: Gravel and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Göttlesbrunn (municipality Göttlesbrunn-Arbesthal), with about 20 ha delimited.

at-grossau-lindenberg.name: Ried Lindenberg
at-grossau-lindenberg.summary: A large Bad Vöslau Ried with many named subrieden, giving red and white wines; Vöslau was a historic red-wine town.
at-grossau-lindenberg.terroir: Limestone and gravel on the slopes of the Vienna Woods. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Großau (municipality Bad Vöslau), with about 30 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Heiliger Berg, Predler, Rauhe Bühel, Sonnberg.

at-grossau-lindenberg-heiliger-berg.name: Ried Lindenberg Heiliger Berg
at-grossau-lindenberg-heiliger-berg.summary: Heiliger Berg is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Lindenberg at Großau, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A large Bad Vöslau Ried with many named subrieden, giving red and white wines; Vöslau was a historic red-wine town.
at-grossau-lindenberg-heiliger-berg.terroir: Limestone and gravel on the slopes of the Vienna Woods.
at-grossau-lindenberg-heiliger-berg.nerd_note: See the Ried Lindenberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-grossau-lindenberg-predler.name: Ried Lindenberg Predler
at-grossau-lindenberg-predler.summary: Predler is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Lindenberg at Großau, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A large Bad Vöslau Ried with many named subrieden, giving red and white wines; Vöslau was a historic red-wine town.
at-grossau-lindenberg-predler.terroir: Limestone and gravel on the slopes of the Vienna Woods.
at-grossau-lindenberg-predler.nerd_note: See the Ried Lindenberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-grossau-lindenberg-rauhe-buhel.name: Ried Lindenberg Rauhe Bühel
at-grossau-lindenberg-rauhe-buhel.summary: Rauhe Bühel is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Lindenberg at Großau, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A large Bad Vöslau Ried with many named subrieden, giving red and white wines; Vöslau was a historic red-wine town.
at-grossau-lindenberg-rauhe-buhel.terroir: Limestone and gravel on the slopes of the Vienna Woods.
at-grossau-lindenberg-rauhe-buhel.nerd_note: See the Ried Lindenberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-grossau-lindenberg-sonnberg.name: Ried Lindenberg Sonnberg
at-grossau-lindenberg-sonnberg.summary: Sonnberg is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Lindenberg at Großau, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A large Bad Vöslau Ried with many named subrieden, giving red and white wines; Vöslau was a historic red-wine town.
at-grossau-lindenberg-sonnberg.terroir: Limestone and gravel on the slopes of the Vienna Woods.
at-grossau-lindenberg-sonnberg.nerd_note: See the Ried Lindenberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-grosshoflein-durr.name: Ried Dürr
at-grosshoflein-durr.summary: A Großhöflein Ried on dry, stony ground, giving firm reds.
at-grosshoflein-durr.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-grosshoflein-durr.terroir: Limestone and gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Großhöflein, with about 20 ha delimited.

at-grosshoflein-follikberg.name: Ried Föllikberg
at-grosshoflein-follikberg.summary: The Föllikberg is a broad hill at Großhöflein on the southern Leithaberg, giving reds and whites on limestone.
at-grosshoflein-follikberg.terroir: Leitha limestone and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Großhöflein, with about 280 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Furtäcker, Föllig, Fölliger Wald und Heide, Fünfjochfeld, Heide, Herrschaftsbreite.

at-grosshoflein-point.name: Ried Point
at-grosshoflein-point.summary: A Großhöflein Ried on the Leitha hills giving fine reds and whites, including Kollwentz wines.
at-grosshoflein-point.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-grosshoflein-point.terroir: Limestone and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Großhöflein, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-grosshoflein-steinzeilen.name: Ried Steinzeilen
at-grosshoflein-steinzeilen.summary: The Steinzeilen at Großhöflein gives Kollwentz's Blaufränkisch 'Steinzeiler', one of the most admired reds of Burgenland: dense, spicy and long. The Steinzeiler is aged in small oak and released late; it sits with the estate's Point and Föllikberg sites on the southern slopes of the Leitha hills, overlooking the Wulka basin.
at-grosshoflein-steinzeilen.terroir: Leitha limestone and schist with stony topsoil. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Großhöflein, with about 20 ha delimited.
at-grosshoflein-steinzeilen.nerd_note: Andi Kollwentz's family helped prove from the 1980s that Burgenland could make world-class dry reds and whites.

at-grossweikersdorf-hohenberg.name: Ried Hohenberg
at-grossweikersdorf-hohenberg.summary: A Großweikersdorf Ried giving fresh Grüner Veltliner.
at-grossweikersdorf-hohenberg.nerd_note: The Wagram's loess bank runs for some 30 km along the north side of the Danube; its DAC rules put Ried wines at the top of the pyramid, with Grüner Veltliner and the local Roter Veltliner as signature grapes.
at-grossweikersdorf-hohenberg.terroir: Loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Großweikersdorf, with about 20 ha delimited.

at-grossweikersdorf-steinberg.name: Ried Steinberg
at-grossweikersdorf-steinberg.summary: A Wagram Ried classified by the ÖTW, giving firm, mineral Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from stonier soils than the usual loess.
at-grossweikersdorf-steinberg.terroir: Gravel, sand and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Großweikersdorf, with about 30 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Hörndler, Kobelberg.

at-grossweikersdorf-steinberg-horndler.name: Ried Steinberg Hörndler
at-grossweikersdorf-steinberg-horndler.summary: Hörndler is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Steinberg at Großweikersdorf, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Wagram Ried classified by the ÖTW, giving firm, mineral Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from stonier soils than the usual loess.
at-grossweikersdorf-steinberg-horndler.nerd_note: See the Ried Steinberg profile for the site's history and growers.
at-grossweikersdorf-steinberg-horndler.classification: ÖTW Erste Lage (1ÖTW) (as part of the Ried Steinberg)

at-grossweikersdorf-steinberg-kobelberg.name: Ried Steinberg Kobelberg
at-grossweikersdorf-steinberg-kobelberg.summary: Kobelberg is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Steinberg at Großweikersdorf, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Wagram Ried classified by the ÖTW, giving firm, mineral Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from stonier soils than the usual loess.
at-grossweikersdorf-steinberg-kobelberg.nerd_note: See the Ried Steinberg profile for the site's history and growers.
