at-gumpoldskirchen-rasslerin.name: Ried Rasslerin
at-gumpoldskirchen-rasslerin.summary: A Gumpoldskirchen Ried giving spicy Zierfandler and Rotgipfler.
at-gumpoldskirchen-rasslerin.nerd_note: The Thermenregion, south of Vienna, is the home of Zierfandler and Rotgipfler on the limestone slopes near Gumpoldskirchen and of Pinot Noir and St. Laurent on the warm gravel plain around Tattendorf.
at-gumpoldskirchen-rasslerin.terroir: Limestone and loam. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Gumpoldskirchen, with about 20 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Stubenberger.

at-gumpoldskirchen-rasslerin-stubenberge.name: Ried Rasslerin Stubenberger
at-gumpoldskirchen-rasslerin-stubenberge.summary: Stubenberger is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Rasslerin at Gumpoldskirchen, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Gumpoldskirchen Ried giving spicy Zierfandler and Rotgipfler.
at-gumpoldskirchen-rasslerin-stubenberge.nerd_note: See the Ried Rasslerin profile for the site's history and growers.

at-gumpoldskirchen-sonnberg.name: Ried Sonnberg
at-gumpoldskirchen-sonnberg.summary: A Gumpoldskirchen Ried giving aromatic white wines on limestone.
at-gumpoldskirchen-sonnberg.nerd_note: The Thermenregion, south of Vienna, is the home of Zierfandler and Rotgipfler on the limestone slopes near Gumpoldskirchen and of Pinot Noir and St. Laurent on the warm gravel plain around Tattendorf.
at-gumpoldskirchen-sonnberg.terroir: Limestone. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Gumpoldskirchen, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-gumpoldskirchen-wiege.name: Ried Wiege
at-gumpoldskirchen-wiege.summary: A Gumpoldskirchen Ried classified by the ÖTW, on the limestone slopes of the Anninger, giving rich Zierfandler and Rotgipfler.
at-gumpoldskirchen-wiege.nerd_note: The Thermenregion, south of Vienna, is the home of Zierfandler and Rotgipfler on the limestone slopes near Gumpoldskirchen and of Pinot Noir and St. Laurent on the warm gravel plain around Tattendorf.
at-gumpoldskirchen-wiege.terroir: Limestone and calcareous sediments. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Gumpoldskirchen.

at-hadersdorf-am-kamp-sachsenberg.name: Ried Sachsenberg
at-hadersdorf-am-kamp-sachsenberg.summary: A Hadersdorf Ried at the eastern end of the Kamptal, giving ripe Grüner Veltliner.
at-hadersdorf-am-kamp-sachsenberg.nerd_note: Kamptal DAC (since 2008) puts Ried-designated Grüner Veltliner and Riesling at the top of its origin pyramid, above village and regional wines.
at-hadersdorf-am-kamp-sachsenberg.terroir: Loess and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Hadersdorf am Kamp (municipality Hadersdorf-Kammern), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-haindorf-hasel.name: Ried Hasel
at-haindorf-hasel.summary: A Ried named after hazel bushes, giving supple Grüner Veltliner on loess.
at-haindorf-hasel.nerd_note: Kamptal DAC (since 2008) puts Ried-designated Grüner Veltliner and Riesling at the top of its origin pyramid, above village and regional wines.
at-haindorf-hasel.terroir: Loess and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Haindorf (municipality Langenlois), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-haindorf-kogelberg.name: Ried Kogelberg
at-haindorf-kogelberg.summary: A Ried on the hills west of Langenlois, giving fresh Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
at-haindorf-kogelberg.nerd_note: Kamptal DAC (since 2008) puts Ried-designated Grüner Veltliner and Riesling at the top of its origin pyramid, above village and regional wines.
at-haindorf-kogelberg.terroir: Gneiss and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Haindorf (municipality Langenlois).

at-haindorf-seeberg.name: Ried Seeberg
at-haindorf-seeberg.summary: A Langenlois Ried on mixed loess and crystalline rock, giving fine Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
at-haindorf-seeberg.nerd_note: Kamptal DAC (since 2008) puts Ried-designated Grüner Veltliner and Riesling at the top of its origin pyramid, above village and regional wines.
at-haindorf-seeberg.terroir: Loess and gneiss. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Haindorf (municipality Langenlois), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-haindorf-spiegel.name: Ried Spiegel
at-haindorf-spiegel.summary: The Spiegel is a broad loess slope near Langenlois giving creamy, peppery Grüner Veltliner, from Fred Loimer, Jurtschitsch and others.
at-haindorf-spiegel.terroir: Deep loess and loam on south-facing slopes. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Haindorf (municipality Langenlois), with about 20 ha delimited.

at-hoflein-barnreiser.name: Ried Bärnreiser
at-hoflein-barnreiser.summary: The Bärnreiser at Höflein is one of Carnuntum's most famous red sites, the source of dense, age-worthy Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch blends, notably from Philipp Grassl.
at-hoflein-barnreiser.terroir: Loam and gravel over limestone. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Höflein, with about 20 ha delimited.

at-hoflein-kraften.name: Ried Kräften
at-hoflein-kraften.summary: A Höflein Ried giving fruity Zweigelt.
at-hoflein-kraften.nerd_note: Carnuntum DAC (since 2019) is built on Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch reds and on white wines from Grüner Veltliner, Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc.
at-hoflein-kraften.terroir: Loess and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Höflein, with about 20 ha delimited.

at-horitschon-durrau.name: Ried Dürrau
at-horitschon-durrau.summary: The Dürrau at Horitschon is one of the great Blaufränkisch sites of Mittelburgenland, where Franz Reinhard Weninger makes a dense, iron-tinged wine from old vines, farmed biodynamically. Weninger also farms vineyards across the Hungarian border near Sopron, where the same grape is called Kékfrankos.
at-horitschon-durrau.terroir: Heavy, iron-rich loam and clay over gravel, which holds water through dry summers. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Horitschon, with about 110 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Lauspil, Rakitsch, Thurnau.
at-horitschon-durrau.nerd_note: Mittelburgenland became one of Austria's first DACs in 2005, dedicated to Blaufränkisch; the Ödenburg, Landsee and Güns hills shelter it on three sides, and locals call it 'Blaufränkischland'.

at-horitschon-gfanger.name: Ried Gfanger
at-horitschon-gfanger.summary: A Horitschon Ried giving juicy, fruity Blaufränkisch.
at-horitschon-gfanger.nerd_note: Mittelburgenland DAC (since 2005) is dedicated to Blaufränkisch, the grape that covers about half of the district's vineyards.
at-horitschon-gfanger.terroir: Loam and gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Horitschon, with about 160 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Oberer Gfanger.

at-horitschon-hochacker.name: Ried Hochäcker
at-horitschon-hochacker.summary: A Horitschon Ried known for Weninger's Blaufränkisch, fresh and spicy, from loam and gravel.
at-horitschon-hochacker.nerd_note: Mittelburgenland DAC (since 2005) is dedicated to Blaufränkisch, the grape that covers about half of the district's vineyards.
at-horitschon-hochacker.terroir: Loam over gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Horitschon, with about 190 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Edelgrund, Kapelln, Kirchholz.

at-imbach-pfeningberg.name: Ried Pfeningberg
at-imbach-pfeningberg.summary: A Senftenberg-area Ried on crystalline rock, giving taut Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-imbach-pfeningberg.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-imbach-pfeningberg.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist with the subrieden Gaisruck and Kiesling. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Imbach (municipality Senftenberg), with about 50 ha delimited.

at-imbach-pfeningberg-gaisruck.name: Ried Pfeningberg Gaisruck
at-imbach-pfeningberg-gaisruck.summary: Gaisruck is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Pfeningberg at Imbach, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Senftenberg-area Ried on crystalline rock, giving taut Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-imbach-pfeningberg-gaisruck.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist with the subrieden Gaisruck and Kiesling.
at-imbach-pfeningberg-gaisruck.nerd_note: See the Ried Pfeningberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-imbach-pfeningberg-kiesling.name: Ried Pfeningberg Kiesling
at-imbach-pfeningberg-kiesling.summary: Kiesling is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Pfeningberg at Imbach, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Senftenberg-area Ried on crystalline rock, giving taut Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-imbach-pfeningberg-kiesling.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist with the subrieden Gaisruck and Kiesling.
at-imbach-pfeningberg-kiesling.nerd_note: See the Ried Pfeningberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-inzersdorf-an-der-traisen-pletzengrab.name: Ried Pletzengraben
at-inzersdorf-an-der-traisen-pletzengrab.summary: The Pletzengraben is a cool, high Ried in the hills of the Traisental, one of Austria's smallest DACs, on the south side of the Danube. Its chalky conglomerate soils give Grüner Veltliner and Riesling with a cool, salty precision. It is one of the highest sites of the Traisental.
at-inzersdorf-an-der-traisen-pletzengrab.terroir: Calcareous conglomerate and gravel at around 350 m, south-facing; the cool air of the Alpine foothills reaches the valley at night. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Inzersdorf an der Traisen (municipality Inzersdorf-Getzersdorf), with about 10 ha delimited.
at-inzersdorf-an-der-traisen-pletzengrab.nerd_note: The Traisental's limestone-rich gravels, deposited by the ancient Traisen river, set it apart from the gneiss and loess of the Danube sites to the north.

at-inzersdorf-an-der-traisen-rafasetzen.name: Ried Rafasetzen
at-inzersdorf-an-der-traisen-rafasetzen.summary: An Inzersdorf Ried where Ludwig Neumayer grows fine Grüner Veltliner.
at-inzersdorf-an-der-traisen-rafasetzen.nerd_note: Traisental DAC (since 2006) covers Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from one of the smallest wine areas of Lower Austria, on the south side of the Danube.
at-inzersdorf-an-der-traisen-rafasetzen.terroir: Conglomerate and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Inzersdorf an der Traisen (municipality Inzersdorf-Getzersdorf), with about 20 ha delimited.

at-inzersdorf-an-der-traisen-zwirch.name: Ried Zwirch
at-inzersdorf-an-der-traisen-zwirch.summary: A steep Inzersdorf Ried of conglomerate rock where Ludwig Neumayer makes taut, chalky Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
at-inzersdorf-an-der-traisen-zwirch.terroir: Calcareous conglomerate with thin soil. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Inzersdorf an der Traisen (municipality Inzersdorf-Getzersdorf), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-joching-jochinger-berg.name: Ried Jochinger Berg
at-joching-jochinger-berg.summary: The hill behind Joching, giving mineral Riesling and Grüner Veltliner from terraced slopes.
at-joching-jochinger-berg.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
at-joching-jochinger-berg.terroir: Gneiss and amphibolite. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Joching (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 30 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Postaller.

at-joching-jochinger-berg-postaller.name: Ried Jochinger Berg Postaller
at-joching-jochinger-berg-postaller.summary: Postaller is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Jochinger Berg at Joching, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The hill behind Joching, giving mineral Riesling and Grüner Veltliner from terraced slopes.
at-joching-jochinger-berg-postaller.nerd_note: See the Ried Jochinger Berg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-joching-kollmitz.name: Ried Kollmitz
at-joching-kollmitz.summary: A small Ried between Joching and Wösendorf, giving fine, aromatic Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
at-joching-kollmitz.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
at-joching-kollmitz.terroir: Gneiss and loess terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Joching (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 20 ha delimited.

at-joching-pichl-point.name: Ried Pichl Point
at-joching-pichl-point.summary: A Joching Ried on gentler slopes near the Danube, giving round, spicy Grüner Veltliner.
at-joching-pichl-point.terroir: Loess and sand over gneiss. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Joching (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 10 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Pichl.

at-joching-pichl-point-pichl.name: Ried Pichl Point Pichl
at-joching-pichl-point-pichl.summary: Pichl is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Pichl Point at Joching, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Joching Ried on gentler slopes near the Danube, giving round, spicy Grüner Veltliner.
at-joching-pichl-point-pichl.nerd_note: See the Ried Pichl Point profile for the site's history and growers.

at-joching-steinriegl.name: Ried Steinriegl
at-joching-steinriegl.summary: The Steinriegl ('stone ridge') climbs high behind Weißenkirchen, one of the coolest top sites of the village thanks to its altitude and the winds that drop out of the Waldviertel forest at night. Prager and Domäne Wachau make sleek, perfumed Riesling here. Its height has made it one of the Wachau's winners as summers have grown warmer: the wines keep their freshness in vintages when the river-side sites turn heavy.
at-joching-steinriegl.terroir: Terraces of gneiss and mica schist rising to over 400 m, south-facing; cooler nights than the river-side sites. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Joching (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau).

at-joching-steinwand.name: Ried Steinwand
at-joching-steinwand.summary: The Steinwand ('stone wall') is a steep terraced site giving stony, concentrated Riesling.
at-joching-steinwand.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
at-joching-steinwand.terroir: Gneiss and amphibolite rock with thin soil. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Joching (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-jois-backobel.name: Ried Backobel
at-jois-backobel.summary: A Jois Ried bottled as a single vineyard by Kiss, giving taut, mineral Blaufränkisch.
at-jois-backobel.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-jois-backobel.terroir: Mica schist and limestone. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Jois, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-jois-hackelsberg.name: Ried Hackelsberg
at-jois-hackelsberg.summary: The Hackelsberg at Jois is a dry, rocky hill and nature reserve with steppe flora above the lake; its vines give spicy Blaufränkisch and firm whites.
at-jois-hackelsberg.terroir: Mica schist and limestone with thin soils. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Jois, with about 30 ha delimited.

at-jois-jungenberg.name: Ried Jungenberg
at-jois-jungenberg.summary: A Jois Ried on the northern Leitha hills where Rudolf and Verena Kiss make fine, cool Blaufränkisch, part of a new wave of Leithaberg growers.
at-jois-jungenberg.terroir: Schist and limestone on south-facing slopes above Lake Neusiedl. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Jois, with about 40 ha delimited.
at-jois-jungenberg.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.

at-jois-ladisberg.name: Ried Ladisberg
at-jois-ladisberg.summary: A Jois Ried on the slopes of the Leitha hills, giving spicy Blaufränkisch and fresh whites.
at-jois-ladisberg.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-jois-ladisberg.terroir: Schist and limestone. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Jois, with about 20 ha delimited.

at-jois-schieferberg.name: Ried Schieferberg
at-jois-schieferberg.summary: A Jois Ried named after its slate ('Schiefer'), giving mineral Blaufränkisch.
at-jois-schieferberg.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-jois-schieferberg.terroir: Mica schist. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Jois, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-jois-tannenberg.name: Ried Tannenberg
at-jois-tannenberg.summary: A Jois Ried giving fresh reds and whites.
at-jois-tannenberg.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-jois-tannenberg.terroir: Schist and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Jois, with about 30 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Buschenberg, Ruissland.

at-kammern-gaisberg.name: Ried Gaisberg
at-kammern-gaisberg.summary: The Kammern side of the Gaisberg, crystalline gneiss and mica schist giving fine, floral Riesling, notably from Hirsch and Schloss Gobelsburg.
at-kammern-gaisberg.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Kammern (municipality Hadersdorf-Kammern), with about 40 ha delimited.

at-kammern-grub.name: Ried Grub
at-kammern-grub.summary: The Grub at Kammern gives a peppery, mid-weight Grüner Veltliner on loess, notably from Hirsch and Schloss Gobelsburg.
at-kammern-grub.terroir: Loess over gravel on gentle slopes. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Kammern (municipality Hadersdorf-Kammern), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-kammern-heiligenstein.name: Ried Heiligenstein
at-kammern-heiligenstein.summary: The Kammern end of the Heiligenstein, a small piece of the famous Permian sandstone hill above Zöbing. Its Rieslings share the spicy, salty profile of the main site.
at-kammern-heiligenstein.terroir: Permian sandstone and conglomerate on the eastern flank of the hill. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Kammern (municipality Hadersdorf-Kammern).

at-kammern-lamm.name: Ried Lamm
at-kammern-lamm.summary: The Lamm lies at the south-eastern foot of the Heiligenstein and is planted almost entirely to Grüner Veltliner. Deep loess and loam over the hill's sandstone give opulent, creamy, spicy wines that rank with the most powerful Veltliners of Austria. Schloss Gobelsburg, Bründlmayer, Hirsch and Jurtschitsch bottle it. In warm years Lamm Grüner Veltliner can reach 14 percent alcohol yet stay balanced. Schloss Gobelsburg, leased from the Cistercians of Zwettl abbey by Michael Moosbrugger since 1996, makes one of the most celebrated versions.
at-kammern-lamm.terroir: About 25 ha of loess and loam with sandstone near the top, rising to about 280 m; very warm but well ventilated. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Kammern (municipality Hadersdorf-Kammern), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-kammern-renner.name: Ried Renner
at-kammern-renner.summary: The Renner below Gobelsburg gives a finely balanced Grüner Veltliner, a long-time favourite of Schloss Gobelsburg.
at-kammern-renner.terroir: Loess and gravel on a gentle south-facing slope. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Kammern (municipality Hadersdorf-Kammern), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-kohfidisch-csaterberg.name: Ried Csaterberg
at-kohfidisch-csaterberg.summary: The Csaterberg at Kohfidisch is a small hill with old cellar houses and a traditional wine village atmosphere, giving spicy Blaufränkisch.
at-kohfidisch-csaterberg.terroir: Green schist and loam, around 280 to 350 m. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Kohfidisch, with about 110 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Hoch Csater, Klein Csater.

at-krems-gebling.name: Ried Gebling
at-krems-gebling.summary: The Krems part of the Gebling, a broad loess hill shared with Rohrendorf, giving ripe Grüner Veltliner.
at-krems-gebling.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-krems-gebling.terroir: Deep loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Krems (municipality Krems an der Donau), with about 40 ha delimited.

at-krems-kogl.name: Ried Kögl
at-krems-kogl.summary: The Kögl is a high site above Krems where Salomon Undhof makes a delicate, peppery Grüner Veltliner.
at-krems-kogl.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-krems-kogl.terroir: Loess over gneiss. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Krems (municipality Krems an der Donau), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-krems-kremsleithen.name: Ried Kremsleithen
at-krems-kremsleithen.summary: A steep Ried on the slopes above the Krems river, giving mineral Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-krems-kremsleithen.terroir: Gneiss and loess, with the subried Kraxen. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Krems (municipality Krems an der Donau), with about 40 ha delimited.

at-krems-kremsleithen-kraxen.name: Ried Kremsleithen Kraxen
at-krems-kremsleithen-kraxen.summary: Kraxen is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Kremsleithen at Krems, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A steep Ried on the slopes above the Krems river, giving mineral Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-krems-kremsleithen-kraxen.terroir: Gneiss and loess, with the subried Kraxen.
at-krems-kremsleithen-kraxen.nerd_note: See the Ried Kremsleithen profile for the site's history and growers.

at-krems-obere-sandgrube.name: Ried Obere Sandgrube
at-krems-obere-sandgrube.summary: The Sandgrube ('sand pit') east of Krems is one of Austria's best-known Grüner Veltliner names, thanks to the Winzer Krems cooperative's 'Sandgrube 13'. The loess and sand here give juicy, peppery Veltliner.
at-krems-obere-sandgrube.terroir: Loess and sand on gentle slopes; the subried Frechau is named on the map. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Krems (municipality Krems an der Donau), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-krems-obere-sandgrube-frechau.name: Ried Obere Sandgrube Frechau
at-krems-obere-sandgrube-frechau.summary: Frechau is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Obere Sandgrube at Krems, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Sandgrube ('sand pit') east of Krems is one of Austria's best-known Grüner Veltliner names, thanks to the Winzer Krems cooperative's 'Sandgrube 13'. The loess and sand here give juicy, peppery Veltliner.
at-krems-obere-sandgrube-frechau.terroir: Loess and sand on gentle slopes; the subried Frechau is named on the map.
at-krems-obere-sandgrube-frechau.nerd_note: Frechau is a historic parcel name within the famous Kremser Sandgrube loess area.

at-krems-thurnerberg.name: Ried Thurnerberg
at-krems-thurnerberg.summary: A high Ried above Krems and Rehberg, giving cool, fresh Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
at-krems-thurnerberg.terroir: Gneiss and loess at about 300 m. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Krems (municipality Krems an der Donau), with about 40 ha delimited.

at-krems-wachtberg.name: Ried Wachtberg
at-krems-wachtberg.summary: The Wachtberg rises above the old town of Krems, a terraced site that the Weingut Stadt Krems (owned by the town since the fifteenth century) has made its flagship. The Grüner Veltliner is dense and spicy, the Riesling fine and stony. From the terraces you look down on the roofs of Krems and the old Steiner Tor; Weingut Stadt Krems, founded in 1452, is one of the oldest wine estates of Austria.
at-krems-wachtberg.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist terraces with loess pockets, facing south over the Krems valley. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Krems (municipality Krems an der Donau), with about 40 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Lindberg.
at-krems-wachtberg.nerd_note: Krems was a medieval wine-trading city; the town estate's vineyards include plots documented since the Middle Ages.

at-krems-wachtberg-lindberg.name: Ried Wachtberg Lindberg
at-krems-wachtberg-lindberg.summary: Lindberg is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Wachtberg at Krems, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Wachtberg rises above the old town of Krems, a terraced site that the Weingut Stadt Krems (owned by the town since the fifteenth century) has made its flagship. The Grüner Veltliner is dense and spicy, the Riesling fine and stony.
at-krems-wachtberg-lindberg.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist terraces with loess pockets, facing south over the Krems valley.
at-krems-wachtberg-lindberg.nerd_note: See the Ried Wachtberg profile for the site's history and growers.
at-krems-wachtberg-lindberg.classification: ÖTW Erste Lage (1ÖTW) (as part of the Ried Wachtberg)

at-krems-weinzierlberg.name: Ried Weinzierlberg
at-krems-weinzierlberg.summary: The Weinzierlberg rises on the edge of Krems towards the Danube plain, giving fresh, peppery Grüner Veltliner; it is classified by the ÖTW.
at-krems-weinzierlberg.terroir: Loess and gneiss on south-facing slopes. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Krems (municipality Krems an der Donau), with about 50 ha delimited.

at-langenlois-dechant.name: Ried Dechant
at-langenlois-dechant.summary: A Langenlois Ried named after a dean (Dechant) who once owned it, giving elegant Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
at-langenlois-dechant.nerd_note: Kamptal DAC (since 2008) puts Ried-designated Grüner Veltliner and Riesling at the top of its origin pyramid, above village and regional wines.
at-langenlois-dechant.terroir: Loess and gneiss. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Langenlois, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-langenlois-hasel.name: Ried Hasel
at-langenlois-hasel.summary: A Ried named after hazel bushes, giving supple Grüner Veltliner on loess.
at-langenlois-hasel.nerd_note: Kamptal DAC (since 2008) puts Ried-designated Grüner Veltliner and Riesling at the top of its origin pyramid, above village and regional wines.
at-langenlois-hasel.terroir: Loess and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Langenlois, with about 60 ha delimited.

at-langenlois-kaferberg.name: Ried Käferberg
at-langenlois-kaferberg.summary: The Käferberg ('beetle hill') rises east of Langenlois, a high site where Bründlmayer and Jurtschitsch make some of the Kamptal's most refined Grüner Veltliner: spicy, deep and long. Langenlois is Austria's largest wine town by vineyard area, and the Käferberg is one of the high, crowning sites on its eastern side, with loess on the lower slope and crystalline rock near the top. Bründlmayer ages its Käferberg in large old oak.
at-langenlois-kaferberg.terroir: Loess and loam over gneiss and amphibolite at around 300 m and above, on south-facing slopes. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Langenlois, with about 40 ha delimited.

at-langenlois-kittmannsberg.name: Ried Kittmannsberg
at-langenlois-kittmannsberg.summary: The Kittmannsberg is a large, high site between Langenlois and Lengenfeld, giving cool, aromatic Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-langenlois-kittmannsberg.terroir: Gneiss and loess at about 270 to 340 m. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Langenlois, with about 100 ha delimited.

at-langenlois-loiserberg.name: Ried Loiserberg
at-langenlois-loiserberg.summary: The Loiserberg is the highest of the Langenlois hills, rising to over 350 m north of the town. Its crystalline soils and cool winds give slender, aromatic Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-langenlois-loiserberg.terroir: Gneiss, granite and mica schist with thin soils; one of the coolest Kamptal sites. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Langenlois, with about 80 ha delimited.

at-langenlois-panzaun.name: Ried Panzaun
at-langenlois-panzaun.summary: A Langenlois Ried on loess giving round Grüner Veltliner.
at-langenlois-panzaun.nerd_note: Kamptal DAC (since 2008) puts Ried-designated Grüner Veltliner and Riesling at the top of its origin pyramid, above village and regional wines.
at-langenlois-panzaun.terroir: Loess and loam. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Langenlois, with about 40 ha delimited.

at-langenlois-schenkenbichl.name: Ried Schenkenbichl
at-langenlois-schenkenbichl.summary: A Langenlois site where Jurtschitsch makes a fine, savoury Grüner Veltliner.
at-langenlois-schenkenbichl.nerd_note: Kamptal DAC (since 2008) puts Ried-designated Grüner Veltliner and Riesling at the top of its origin pyramid, above village and regional wines.
at-langenlois-schenkenbichl.terroir: Loess and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Langenlois, with about 30 ha delimited.

at-langenlois-seeberg.name: Ried Seeberg
at-langenlois-seeberg.summary: A Langenlois Ried on mixed loess and crystalline rock, giving fine Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
at-langenlois-seeberg.nerd_note: Kamptal DAC (since 2008) puts Ried-designated Grüner Veltliner and Riesling at the top of its origin pyramid, above village and regional wines.
at-langenlois-seeberg.terroir: Loess and gneiss. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Langenlois, with about 40 ha delimited.

at-langenlois-spiegel.name: Ried Spiegel
at-langenlois-spiegel.summary: The Spiegel is a broad loess slope near Langenlois giving creamy, peppery Grüner Veltliner, from Fred Loimer, Jurtschitsch and others.
at-langenlois-spiegel.terroir: Deep loess and loam on south-facing slopes. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Langenlois, with about 40 ha delimited.

at-langenlois-steinhaus.name: Ried Steinhaus
at-langenlois-steinhaus.summary: A Langenlois Ried giving fresh Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
at-langenlois-steinhaus.nerd_note: Kamptal DAC (since 2008) puts Ried-designated Grüner Veltliner and Riesling at the top of its origin pyramid, above village and regional wines.
at-langenlois-steinhaus.terroir: Loess and gneiss. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Langenlois, with about 40 ha delimited.

at-langenlois-steinmassl.name: Ried Steinmassl
at-langenlois-steinmassl.summary: The Steinmassl is a stony, cool Langenlois site where gneiss and mica schist sit close to the surface. Bründlmayer and Fred Loimer make delicate, floral, very mineral Riesling here. The soils warm slowly in spring, so the site buds and ripens later than the loess slopes below; its Rieslings are among the most delicate of the Kamptal, with white flowers and lime. Fred Loimer farms biodynamically.
at-langenlois-steinmassl.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist with little loess, south-facing at around 300 m. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Langenlois, with about 40 ha delimited.

at-lengenfeld-kittmannsberg.name: Ried Kittmannsberg
at-lengenfeld-kittmannsberg.summary: The Lengenfeld side of the Kittmannsberg, a cooler, higher slope giving fragrant Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
at-lengenfeld-kittmannsberg.nerd_note: Kamptal DAC (since 2008) puts Ried-designated Grüner Veltliner and Riesling at the top of its origin pyramid, above village and regional wines.
at-lengenfeld-kittmannsberg.terroir: Gneiss and loess at altitude. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Lengenfeld, with about 20 ha delimited.

at-lutzmannsburg-altes-weingebirge.name: Ried Altes Weingebirge
at-lutzmannsburg-altes-weingebirge.summary: The Altes Weingebirge ('old vineyard hill') at Lutzmannsburg on the Hungarian border holds some of the oldest Blaufränkisch vines in Austria; Moric's Lutzmannsburg Alte Reben comes from here and helped redefine the variety after 2001. Roland Velich founded Moric in 2001, rejecting the fashion for heavy oak and extraction in search of a Burgundy-like finesse; his old-vine Lutzmannsburg became one of the most influential Austrian reds of the 2000s.
at-lutzmannsburg-altes-weingebirge.terroir: Loam and gravel over gneiss and schist on gentle slopes. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Lutzmannsburg, with about 60 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Auleiter, Marktweger, Neusatz, Schwemmer.

at-mautern-alte-point.name: Ried Alte Point
at-mautern-alte-point.summary: The Alte Point at Mautern includes the subried Im Weingebirge, the source of Nikolaihof's Grüner Veltliner and Riesling 'Im Weingebirge'.
at-mautern-alte-point.terroir: Loess and gneiss on the south bank. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Mautern (municipality Mautern an der Donau), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-mautern-alte-point-im-weingebirge.name: Ried Alte Point Im Weingebirge
at-mautern-alte-point-im-weingebirge.summary: Im Weingebirge is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Alte Point at Mautern, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Alte Point at Mautern includes the subried Im Weingebirge, the source of Nikolaihof's Grüner Veltliner and Riesling 'Im Weingebirge'.
at-mautern-alte-point-im-weingebirge.terroir: Loess and gneiss on the south bank.
at-mautern-alte-point-im-weingebirge.nerd_note: This is the source of Nikolaihof's Grüner Veltliner and Riesling 'Im Weingebirge'.

at-mautern-bischofpoint.name: Ried Bischofpoint
at-mautern-bischofpoint.summary: A Mautern Ried whose name recalls episcopal ownership; Bavarian bishoprics and abbeys such as Passau, Freising and Tegernsee held much of the Wachau's vineyard land in the Middle Ages.
at-mautern-bischofpoint.terroir: Loess and gneiss. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Mautern (municipality Mautern an der Donau), with about 20 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Leukuschberg.

at-mautern-bischofpoint-leukuschberg.name: Ried Bischofpoint Leukuschberg
at-mautern-bischofpoint-leukuschberg.summary: Leukuschberg is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Bischofpoint at Mautern, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Mautern Ried whose name recalls episcopal ownership; Bavarian bishoprics and abbeys such as Passau, Freising and Tegernsee held much of the Wachau's vineyard land in the Middle Ages.
at-mautern-bischofpoint-leukuschberg.nerd_note: See the Ried Bischofpoint profile for the site's history and growers.

at-mautern-silberbichl.name: Ried Silberbichl
at-mautern-silberbichl.summary: The Silberbichl at Mautern is the source of Nikolaihof's Riesling 'Vom Stein', a famously long-lived dry wine. Nikolaihof is often called Austria's oldest wine estate: its buildings stand on the walls of the Roman fort of Favianis, and the estate has farmed biodynamically since 1971. Mautern lies on the south bank opposite Stein, and its vineyards face the Danube from the other side, a cooler, later-ripening exposure.
at-mautern-silberbichl.terroir: Gneiss and gravel on the south bank of the Danube; the subried Silberbichl Vom Stein is named on the map. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Mautern (municipality Mautern an der Donau), with about 50 ha delimited.
at-mautern-silberbichl.nerd_note: Nikolaihof ages some Rieslings for many years in old casks before release, the 'Vinothek' bottlings.

at-mautern-silberbichl-vom-stein.name: Ried Silberbichl Vom Stein
at-mautern-silberbichl-vom-stein.summary: Vom Stein is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Silberbichl at Mautern, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Silberbichl at Mautern is the source of Nikolaihof's Riesling 'Vom Stein', a famously long-lived dry wine. Nikolaihof is often called Austria's oldest wine estate: its buildings stand on the walls of the Roman fort of Favianis, and the estate has farmed biodynamically since 1971.
at-mautern-silberbichl-vom-stein.terroir: Gneiss and gravel on the south bank of the Danube; the subried Silberbichl Vom Stein is named on the map.
at-mautern-silberbichl-vom-stein.nerd_note: This is the source of Nikolaihof's Riesling 'Vom Stein', one of the longest-lived dry whites of Austria.

at-mittelberg-loiserberg.name: Ried Loiserberg
at-mittelberg-loiserberg.summary: The Loiserberg is the highest of the Langenlois hills, rising to over 350 m north of the town. Its crystalline soils and cool winds give slender, aromatic Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-mittelberg-loiserberg.terroir: Gneiss, granite and mica schist with thin soils; one of the coolest Kamptal sites. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Mittelberg (municipality Langenlois), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-mitterstockstall-schlossberg.name: Ried Schlossberg
at-mitterstockstall-schlossberg.summary: The Schlossberg at Oberstockstall is where Karl Fritsch grows his top Riesling and Grüner Veltliner, biodynamically farmed and among the finest of the Wagram.
at-mitterstockstall-schlossberg.terroir: Loess and gravel with some crystalline rock. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Mitterstockstall (municipality Kirchberg am Wagram), with about 80 ha delimited.

at-neckenmarkt-bergleiten.name: Ried Bergleiten
at-neckenmarkt-bergleiten.summary: A Neckenmarkt Ried on the slopes of the hills, giving spicy Blaufränkisch.
at-neckenmarkt-bergleiten.nerd_note: Mittelburgenland DAC (since 2005) is dedicated to Blaufränkisch, the grape that covers about half of the district's vineyards.
at-neckenmarkt-bergleiten.terroir: Schist and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Neckenmarkt, with about 40 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Oberläng, Weißer Weg.

at-neckenmarkt-hochberg.name: Ried Hochberg
at-neckenmarkt-hochberg.summary: The Hochberg rises above Neckenmarkt to nearly 380 m, a cool, schist-rich slope whose old-vine Blaufränkisch is among the finest of the district; Moric's Neckenmarkt Alte Reben comes from old vines in this village.
at-neckenmarkt-hochberg.terroir: Mica schist and gneiss with loam, unusual in a district dominated by heavy clay. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Neckenmarkt, with about 200 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Bodigraben, Himmelsthron, Himmelsthron (Burgstall), Hochgrunderitsch, Kohlenberg, Mittergrunderitsch.

at-neusiedl-gaisruck.name: Ried Gaisruck
at-neusiedl-gaisruck.summary: A Ried on the Nußdorf hills giving fresh white wines.
at-neusiedl-gaisruck.nerd_note: Traisental DAC (since 2006) covers Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from one of the smallest wine areas of Lower Austria, on the south side of the Danube.
at-neusiedl-gaisruck.terroir: Conglomerate and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Neusiedl (municipality Nußdorf ob der Traisen), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-neusiedl-hochschopf.name: Ried Hochschopf
at-neusiedl-hochschopf.summary: A Ried on the hills of Nußdorf ob der Traisen, giving fresh, mineral Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
at-neusiedl-hochschopf.terroir: Calcareous gravel and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Neusiedl (municipality Nußdorf ob der Traisen), with about 40 ha delimited.

at-nussdorf-an-der-traisen-gaisruck.name: Ried Gaisruck
at-nussdorf-an-der-traisen-gaisruck.summary: A Ried on the Nußdorf hills giving fresh white wines.
at-nussdorf-an-der-traisen-gaisruck.nerd_note: Traisental DAC (since 2006) covers Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from one of the smallest wine areas of Lower Austria, on the south side of the Danube.
at-nussdorf-an-der-traisen-gaisruck.terroir: Conglomerate and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Nußdorf an der Traisen (municipality Nußdorf ob der Traisen), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-nussdorf-an-der-traisen-hochschopf.name: Ried Hochschopf
at-nussdorf-an-der-traisen-hochschopf.summary: A Ried on the hills of Nußdorf ob der Traisen, giving fresh, mineral Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.

at-oberfucha-hohlgraben.name: Ried Höhlgraben
at-oberfucha-hohlgraben.summary: A Ried near Palt and Furth, home of Weingut Malat, giving fresh Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.

at-oberloiben-frauenweingarten.name: Ried Frauenweingarten

at-oberndorf-am-gebirge-fuchsenrand.summary: A Ried at Oberndorf near Traismauer, giving fresh Grüner Veltliner.
at-oberndorf-am-gebirge-fuchsenrand.nerd_note: Traisental DAC (since 2006) covers Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from one of the smallest wine areas of Lower Austria, on the south side of the Danube.
at-oberndorf-am-gebirge-fuchsenrand.terroir: Loess and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Oberndorf am Gebirge (municipality Traismauer), with about 20 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Marienruh.

at-oberndorf-am-gebirge-fuchsenrand-mari.name: Ried Fuchsenrand Marienruh
at-oberndorf-am-gebirge-fuchsenrand-mari.summary: Marienruh is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Fuchsenrand at Oberndorf am Gebirge, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Ried at Oberndorf near Traismauer, giving fresh Grüner Veltliner.
at-oberndorf-am-gebirge-fuchsenrand-mari.nerd_note: See the Ried Fuchsenrand profile for the site's history and growers.

at-oberrohrendorf-gebling.name: Ried Gebling
at-oberrohrendorf-gebling.summary: The Gebling at Rohrendorf is a broad loess hill east of Krems, home ground of Lenz Moser, the estate where Laurenz Moser developed the high 'Hochkultur' trellis in the 1920s and 1950s that changed Austrian viticulture.

at-oberstockstall-schlossberg.name: Ried Schlossberg
at-oberstockstall-schlossberg.summary: The Schlossberg at Oberstockstall is where Karl Fritsch grows his top Riesling and Grüner Veltliner, biodynamically farmed and among the finest of the Wagram.
at-oberstockstall-schlossberg.terroir: Loess and gravel with some crystalline rock. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Oberstockstall (municipality Kirchberg am Wagram), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-oggau-am-neusiedler-see-marienthal.name: Ried Marienthal
at-oggau-am-neusiedler-see-marienthal.summary: An Oggau Ried near Rust, giving reds and whites; Oggau is the home of the natural-wine producers Gut Oggau.
at-oggau-am-neusiedler-see-marienthal.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-oggau-am-neusiedler-see-marienthal.terroir: Limestone and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Oggau am Neusiedler See, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-palt-hohlgraben.name: Ried Höhlgraben
at-palt-hohlgraben.summary: A Ried near Palt and Furth, home of Weingut Malat, giving fresh Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.

at-palt-steinbuhel.name: Ried Steinbühel
at-palt-steinbuhel.summary: A Palt Ried giving fine, mineral Grüner Veltliner.
at-palt-steinbuhel.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-palt-steinbuhel.terroir: Gravel and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Palt (municipality Furth bei Göttweig), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-prellenkirchen-spitzerberg.name: Ried Spitzerberg
at-prellenkirchen-spitzerberg.summary: The Spitzerberg is a limestone hill rising out of the plain at Prellenkirchen, close to the Slovak border. It gives Carnuntum's most elegant Blaufränkisch, with a cool, chalky finesse; Dorli Muhr's Muhr-van der Niepoort and Johannes Trapl made it famous after 2000. Dorli Muhr founded the estate with Dirk Niepoort in the early 2000s, returning to her family's home village to revive old vineyards on the hill.
at-prellenkirchen-spitzerberg.terroir: Limestone and calcareous sands on a windy, isolated hill; subrieden include Obere Roterd and Obere Spitzer. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Prellenkirchen, with about 30 ha delimited. Named subrieden: - Obere Roterd, - Obere Spitzer.
at-prellenkirchen-spitzerberg.nerd_note: The hill is a nature reserve, and the vines share it with rare dry-grassland steppe flora.

at-prellenkirchen-spitzerberg-obere-rote.name: Ried Spitzerberg - Obere Roterd
at-prellenkirchen-spitzerberg-obere-rote.summary: Obere Roterd is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Spitzerberg at Prellenkirchen, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Spitzerberg is a limestone hill rising out of the plain at Prellenkirchen, close to the Slovak border. It gives Carnuntum's most elegant Blaufränkisch, with a cool, chalky finesse; Dorli Muhr's Muhr-van der Niepoort and Johannes Trapl made it famous after 2000.
at-prellenkirchen-spitzerberg-obere-rote.terroir: Limestone and calcareous sands on a windy, isolated hill; subrieden include Obere Roterd and Obere Spitzer.
at-prellenkirchen-spitzerberg-obere-rote.nerd_note: Roterd means 'red earth', after the iron-rich soil over the limestone; Muhr-van der Niepoort bottles a Blaufränkisch from it.

at-prellenkirchen-spitzerberg-obere-spit.name: Ried Spitzerberg - Obere Spitzer
at-prellenkirchen-spitzerberg-obere-spit.summary: Obere Spitzer is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Spitzerberg at Prellenkirchen, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. at-prellenkirchen-spitzerberg-obere-spit.nerd_note: See the Ried Spitzerberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-prellenkirchen-untere-roterd.name: Ried Untere Roterd
at-prellenkirchen-untere-roterd.summary: The lower 'red earth' at the foot of the Spitzerberg, giving fine, perfumed Blaufränkisch.
at-prellenkirchen-untere-roterd.nerd_note: Carnuntum DAC (since 2019) is built on Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch reds and on white wines from Grüner Veltliner, Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc.
at-prellenkirchen-untere-roterd.terroir: Iron-rich red loam over limestone. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Prellenkirchen, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-priel-kiesling.name: Ried Kiesling
at-priel-kiesling.summary: A Ried in the Krems valley near Priel, giving fresh Grüner Veltliner.
at-priel-kiesling.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-priel-kiesling.terroir: Gravel and gneiss. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Priel (municipality Senftenberg), with about 30 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Grosser Berg.

at-priel-kiesling-grosser-berg.name: Ried Kiesling Grosser Berg
at-priel-kiesling-grosser-berg.summary: Grosser Berg is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Kiesling at Priel, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Ried in the Krems valley near Priel, giving fresh Grüner Veltliner.
at-priel-kiesling-grosser-berg.nerd_note: See the Ried Kiesling profile for the site's history and growers.

at-priel-pfeningberg.name: Ried Pfeningberg
at-priel-pfeningberg.summary: A Senftenberg-area Ried on crystalline rock, giving taut Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-priel-pfeningberg.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-priel-pfeningberg.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist with the subrieden Gaisruck and Kiesling. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Priel (municipality Senftenberg), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-purbach-am-neusiedler-see-edelberg.name: Ried Edelberg
at-purbach-am-neusiedler-see-edelberg.summary: A Purbach Ried giving fresh, mineral whites and reds.
at-purbach-am-neusiedler-see-edelberg.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-purbach-am-neusiedler-see-edelberg.terroir: Limestone and schist. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Purbach am Neusiedler See, with about 20 ha delimited.

at-purbach-am-neusiedler-see-goldberg.name: Ried Goldberg
at-purbach-am-neusiedler-see-goldberg.summary: A Purbach Ried on the Leitha hills giving firm Blaufränkisch and Pinot Blanc; Purbach is known for its old cellar lane, the Kellergasse.
at-purbach-am-neusiedler-see-goldberg.terroir: Limestone and schist. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Purbach am Neusiedler See, with about 20 ha delimited.

at-purbach-am-neusiedler-see-thenau.name: Ried Thenau
at-purbach-am-neusiedler-see-thenau.summary: A large Ried running down from Purbach towards the lake, giving fruity reds and whites.
at-purbach-am-neusiedler-see-thenau.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-purbach-am-neusiedler-see-thenau.terroir: Loam and gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Purbach am Neusiedler See, with about 80 ha delimited.

at-rehberg-kremser-goldberg.name: Ried Kremser Goldberg
at-rehberg-kremser-goldberg.summary: A Ried above Rehberg in the Krems valley, giving fine, aromatic Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
at-rehberg-kremser-goldberg.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-rehberg-kremser-goldberg.terroir: Gneiss and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Rehberg (municipality Krems an der Donau), with about 50 ha delimited.

at-rehberg-kremsleithen.name: Ried Kremsleithen
at-rehberg-kremsleithen.summary: A steep Ried on the slopes above the Krems river, giving mineral Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-rehberg-kremsleithen.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-rehberg-kremsleithen.terroir: Gneiss and loess, with the subried Kraxen. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Rehberg (municipality Krems an der Donau).

at-rehberg-thurnerberg.name: Ried Thurnerberg
at-rehberg-thurnerberg.summary: A high Ried above Krems and Rehberg, giving cool, fresh Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
at-rehberg-thurnerberg.terroir: Gneiss and loess at about 300 m. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Rehberg (municipality Krems an der Donau), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-reichersdorf-alte-setzen.name: Ried Alte Setzen
at-reichersdorf-alte-setzen.summary: A Reichersdorf Ried where Markus Huber makes a deep, old-vine Grüner Veltliner.
at-reichersdorf-alte-setzen.terroir: Loess and conglomerate, with the subrieden Buchhammer and Rohern. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Reichersdorf (municipality Nußdorf ob der Traisen), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-reichersdorf-alte-setzen-buchhammer.name: Ried Alte Setzen Buchhammer
at-reichersdorf-alte-setzen-buchhammer.summary: Buchhammer is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Alte Setzen at Reichersdorf, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Reichersdorf Ried where Markus Huber makes a deep, old-vine Grüner Veltliner.
at-reichersdorf-alte-setzen-buchhammer.terroir: Loess and conglomerate, with the subrieden Buchhammer and Rohern.
at-reichersdorf-alte-setzen-buchhammer.nerd_note: See the Ried Alte Setzen profile for the site's history and growers.

at-reichersdorf-alte-setzen-rohern.name: Ried Alte Setzen Rohern
at-reichersdorf-alte-setzen-rohern.summary: Rohern is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Alte Setzen at Reichersdorf, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Reichersdorf Ried where Markus Huber makes a deep, old-vine Grüner Veltliner.
