at-reichersdorf-alte-setzen-rohern.nerd_note: See the Ried Alte Setzen profile for the site's history and growers.

at-reichersdorf-spiegeln.name: Ried Spiegeln
at-reichersdorf-spiegeln.summary: A Reichersdorf Ried giving fruity Grüner Veltliner.
at-reichersdorf-spiegeln.nerd_note: Traisental DAC (since 2006) covers Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from one of the smallest wine areas of Lower Austria, on the south side of the Danube.
at-reichersdorf-spiegeln.terroir: Loess and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Reichersdorf (municipality Nußdorf ob der Traisen), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-rossatz-frauenweingarten.name: Ried Frauenweingärten
at-rossatz-frauenweingarten.summary: A Rossatz Ried on the south bank, giving fresh Grüner Veltliner.
at-rossatz-frauenweingarten.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
at-rossatz-frauenweingarten.terroir: Loess and sand. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Rossatz (municipality Rossatz-Arnsdorf), with about 20 ha delimited.

at-rossatz-kirnberg.name: Ried Kirnberg
at-rossatz-kirnberg.summary: A Rossatz Ried on the south bank of the Danube, giving lively, fresh wines; the right bank faces mostly north-west and ripens later.
at-rossatz-kirnberg.terroir: Gneiss and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Rossatz (municipality Rossatz-Arnsdorf), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-rossatz-steiger.name: Ried Steiger
at-rossatz-steiger.summary: A Rossatz Ried on the south bank, giving crisp Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
at-rossatz-steiger.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
at-rossatz-steiger.terroir: Gneiss terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Rossatz (municipality Rossatz-Arnsdorf), with about 20 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Himmelreich.

at-rossatz-steiger-himmelreich.name: Ried Steiger Himmelreich
at-rossatz-steiger-himmelreich.summary: Himmelreich is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Steiger at Rossatz, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Rossatz Ried on the south bank, giving crisp Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
at-rossatz-steiger-himmelreich.nerd_note: See the Ried Steiger profile for the site's history and growers.

at-ruppersthal-mordthal.name: Ried Mordthal
at-ruppersthal-mordthal.summary: The Mordthal ('murder valley') at Ruppersthal is a Wagram Ried classified by the ÖTW, a large site whose best parcels give spicy, deep Grüner Veltliner.
at-ruppersthal-mordthal.terroir: Loess and gravel on south-facing slopes. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Ruppersthal (municipality Großweikersdorf), with about 160 ha delimited.

at-ruppersthal-steinberg.name: Ried Steinberg
at-ruppersthal-steinberg.summary: A Wagram Ried classified by the ÖTW, giving firm, mineral Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from stonier soils than the usual loess.
at-ruppersthal-steinberg.terroir: Gravel, sand and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Ruppersthal (municipality Großweikersdorf), with about 70 ha delimited.

at-rust-gertberg.name: Ried Gertberg
at-rust-gertberg.summary: A Rust Ried on the slopes above the town, giving reds and whites.
at-rust-gertberg.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-rust-gertberg.terroir: Limestone and schist. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Rust, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-rust-greiner.name: Ried Greiner
at-rust-greiner.summary: A low Rust Ried close to the reed belt of the lake, a classic source of botrytis for Ruster Ausbruch.
at-rust-greiner.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-rust-greiner.terroir: Sandy loam near the shore. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Rust, with about 20 ha delimited.

at-rust-mariental.name: Ried Mariental
at-rust-mariental.summary: The Mariental is the Rust site of Ernst Triebaumer whose 1986 Blaufränkisch Mariental helped launch the modern era of Austrian red wine. It gives dense, structured, long-lived Blaufränkisch. The 1986 scored so highly in tastings that it became the benchmark for oak-aged Blaufränkisch; Triebaumer's sons continue the estate. Rust itself is famous for the storks that nest on its chimneys every spring.
at-rust-mariental.terroir: Limestone and schist on a warm slope above the lake. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Rust.

at-rust-plachen.name: Ried Plachen
at-rust-plachen.summary: A Rust Ried giving reds and sweet whites.
at-rust-plachen.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-rust-plachen.terroir: Limestone and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Rust, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-rust-turner.name: Ried Turner
at-rust-turner.summary: A Rust Ried giving rich, sweet and dry whites as well as reds.
at-rust-turner.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-rust-turner.terroir: Limestone and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Rust, with about 20 ha delimited.

at-rust-vogelsang.name: Ried Vogelsang
at-rust-vogelsang.summary: A Rust Ried near the lake, giving whites for Ruster Ausbruch and dry wines; lake mists here encourage noble rot in autumn.
at-rust-vogelsang.terroir: Sandy loam and limestone near the shore. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Rust, with about 40 ha delimited.
at-rust-vogelsang.nerd_note: Rust, the free town on Lake Neusiedl, is famous for Ruster Ausbruch, a botrytised sweet wine that has its own DAC since 2020; the town's grower families bought their royal charter in 1681 with wine and gold.

at-schutzen-am-gebirge-goldberg.name: Ried Goldberg
at-schutzen-am-gebirge-goldberg.summary: The Goldberg at Schützen am Gebirge is the top site of Weingut Prieler, a hill of mica schist whose Blaufränkisch is cool, dense and mineral, among the finest in Austria. Georg Prieler now runs the family estate in Schützen.
at-schutzen-am-gebirge-goldberg.terroir: Mica schist with little topsoil on a south-facing slope of the Leitha hills. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Schützen am Gebirge, with about 20 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Obere Goldberg, Untere Goldberg.
at-schutzen-am-gebirge-goldberg.nerd_note: Prieler's Goldberg was one of the first Austrian Blaufränkisch bottlings to show that schist gives a finer, more mineral style than the loam of the plains.

at-senftenberg-ehrenfels.name: Ried Ehrenfels
at-senftenberg-ehrenfels.summary: A small, rocky Ried below the Senftenberg castle ruin where Proidl makes concentrated, mineral Riesling.
at-senftenberg-ehrenfels.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-senftenberg-ehrenfels.terroir: Gneiss rock with thin soils. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Senftenberg.

at-senftenberg-hochacker.name: Ried Hochäcker
at-senftenberg-hochacker.summary: The Hochäcker is a high, iron-rich gneiss slope at Senftenberg in the Krems valley, first documented in 1425. Martin Nigl and Proidl make piercing, mineral Riesling here, among the coolest and most precise of the Kremstal. Martin Nigl, whose estate sits below the ruins of Senftenberg castle, is one of Austria's leading Riesling specialists; the Krems valley is cooler than the Danube, and Hochäcker Rieslings combine peachy ripeness with high acidity.
at-senftenberg-hochacker.terroir: About 14 ha of weathered gneiss up to about 380 m, with the subried Felsengarten. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Senftenberg, with about 20 ha delimited.

at-senftenberg-hochacker-felsengarten.name: Ried Hochäcker Felsengarten
at-senftenberg-hochacker-felsengarten.summary: Felsengarten is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Hochäcker at Senftenberg, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Hochäcker is a high, iron-rich gneiss slope at Senftenberg in the Krems valley, first documented in 1425. Martin Nigl and Proidl make piercing, mineral Riesling here, among the coolest and most precise of the Kremstal.
at-senftenberg-hochacker-felsengarten.terroir: About 14 ha of weathered gneiss up to about 380 m, with the subried Felsengarten.
at-senftenberg-hochacker-felsengarten.nerd_note: Felsengarten ('rock garden') names the stoniest, most rock-strewn part of the Hochäcker.
at-senftenberg-hochacker-felsengarten.classification: ÖTW Erste Lage (1ÖTW) (as part of the Ried Hochäcker)

at-sooss-lange-bergweingarten.name: Ried Lange Bergweingärten
at-sooss-lange-bergweingarten.summary: A Ried on the hills of Sooß near Baden, giving reds and whites on limestone.
at-sooss-lange-bergweingarten.nerd_note: The Thermenregion, south of Vienna, is the home of Zierfandler and Rotgipfler on the limestone slopes near Gumpoldskirchen and of Pinot Noir and St. Laurent on the warm gravel plain around Tattendorf.
at-sooss-lange-bergweingarten.terroir: Limestone and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Sooß.

at-spitz-1000-eimerberg.name: Ried 1000-Eimerberg
at-spitz-1000-eimerberg.summary: The Tausendeimerberg ('thousand-bucket hill') is the cone-shaped hill at Spitz, so named because it was said to yield a thousand buckets of wine in a good year. It gives fine, perfumed Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-spitz-1000-eimerberg.terroir: Gneiss and amphibolite terraces wrapping around a steep hill. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Spitz, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-spitz-atzberg.name: Ried Atzberg
at-spitz-atzberg.summary: The Atzberg is a steep terraced hill above Spitz that was abandoned for decades and replanted in the 2000s, a symbol of the effort to save the Wachau's highest terraces.
at-spitz-atzberg.terroir: Gneiss terraces rising steeply above the village. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Spitz.

at-spitz-axpoint.name: Ried Axpoint
at-spitz-axpoint.summary: The Axpoint at Spitz is known for Franz Hirtzberger's generous, peppery Grüner Veltliner, grown on loess and gneiss.
at-spitz-axpoint.terroir: Loess over gneiss on lower terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Spitz, with about 10 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Hochrain.

at-spitz-axpoint-hochrain.name: Ried Axpoint Hochrain
at-spitz-axpoint-hochrain.summary: Hochrain is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Axpoint at Spitz, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Axpoint at Spitz is known for Franz Hirtzberger's generous, peppery Grüner Veltliner, grown on loess and gneiss.
at-spitz-axpoint-hochrain.terroir: Loess over gneiss on lower terraces.
at-spitz-axpoint-hochrain.nerd_note: See the Ried Axpoint profile for the site's history and growers.

at-spitz-burgberg.name: Ried Burgberg
at-spitz-burgberg.summary: The hill around the castle ruin above Spitz, giving fine Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-spitz-burgberg.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
at-spitz-burgberg.terroir: Gneiss terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Spitz, with about 10 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Schlossgarten.

at-spitz-burgberg-schlossgarten.name: Ried Burgberg Schlossgarten
at-spitz-burgberg-schlossgarten.summary: Schlossgarten is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Burgberg at Spitz, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The hill around the castle ruin above Spitz, giving fine Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-spitz-burgberg-schlossgarten.nerd_note: See the Ried Burgberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-spitz-hartberg.name: Ried Hartberg
at-spitz-hartberg.summary: A high Spitz Ried at around 400 m, giving cool, taut wines.
at-spitz-hartberg.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
at-spitz-hartberg.terroir: Gneiss terraces at altitude. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Spitz, with about 20 ha delimited.

at-spitz-offenberg.name: Ried Offenberg
at-spitz-offenberg.summary: A Spitz Ried giving cool, mineral Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-spitz-offenberg.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
at-spitz-offenberg.terroir: Gneiss terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Spitz, with about 10 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Almenreith.

at-spitz-offenberg-almenreith.name: Ried Offenberg Almenreith
at-spitz-offenberg-almenreith.summary: Almenreith is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Offenberg at Spitz, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Spitz Ried giving cool, mineral Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-spitz-offenberg-almenreith.nerd_note: See the Ried Offenberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-spitz-setzberg.name: Ried Setzberg
at-spitz-setzberg.summary: The Setzberg runs above Spitz towards the Spitzer Graben, a cool site whose wines are taut and floral; the subrieden Landstallen and Vogelsang are named on the official map.
at-spitz-setzberg.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist terraces, south facing. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Spitz, with about 40 ha delimited.

at-spitz-setzberg-landstallen.name: Ried Setzberg Landstallen
at-spitz-setzberg-landstallen.summary: Landstallen is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Setzberg at Spitz, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Setzberg runs above Spitz towards the Spitzer Graben, a cool site whose wines are taut and floral; the subrieden Landstallen and Vogelsang are named on the official map.
at-spitz-setzberg-landstallen.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist terraces, south facing.
at-spitz-setzberg-landstallen.nerd_note: See the Ried Setzberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-spitz-setzberg-vogelsang.name: Ried Setzberg Vogelsang
at-spitz-setzberg-vogelsang.summary: Vogelsang is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Setzberg at Spitz, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Setzberg runs above Spitz towards the Spitzer Graben, a cool site whose wines are taut and floral; the subrieden Landstallen and Vogelsang are named on the official map.
at-spitz-setzberg-vogelsang.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist terraces, south facing.
at-spitz-setzberg-vogelsang.nerd_note: See the Ried Setzberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-spitz-singerriedel.name: Ried Singerriedel
at-spitz-singerriedel.summary: The Singerriedel is the steep amphitheatre of terraces directly behind Spitz, rising above the church. Franz Hirtzberger's Riesling Smaragd from here is one of Austria's iconic white wines, aromatic and silky with a cool, stony core. The site is cooler than the Loibenberg because Spitz sits at the upstream end of the Wachau, where the valley narrows and air from the Waldviertel flows down at night.
at-spitz-singerriedel.terroir: Gneiss and paragneiss terraces from the village up to around 450 m, south to south-east facing, with very thin topsoil. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Spitz, with about 10 ha delimited.
at-spitz-singerriedel.nerd_note: Spitz is the last wine village of the Wachau's north bank before the valley turns into the cool Spitzer Graben, which is why its wines are finer-boned than Loiben's.

at-spitz-steinporz.name: Ried Steinporz
at-spitz-steinporz.summary: A Spitz Ried of rocky terraces, giving stony, aromatic Riesling.
at-spitz-steinporz.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
at-spitz-steinporz.terroir: Gneiss rock with thin soils. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Spitz, with about 20 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Gasselreith.

at-spitz-steinporz-gasselreith.name: Ried Steinporz Gasselreith
at-spitz-steinporz-gasselreith.summary: Gasselreith is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Steinporz at Spitz, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Spitz Ried of rocky terraces, giving stony, aromatic Riesling.
at-spitz-steinporz-gasselreith.nerd_note: See the Ried Steinporz profile for the site's history and growers.

at-spitz-zornberg.name: Ried Zornberg
at-spitz-zornberg.summary: A Spitz Ried giving fresh, aromatic wines.
at-spitz-zornberg.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
at-spitz-zornberg.terroir: Gneiss and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Spitz, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-st-michael-harzenleiten.name: Ried Harzenleiten
at-st-michael-harzenleiten.summary: A Ried at St. Michael, the village with the oldest church of the Wachau, giving fresh Grüner Veltliner.
at-st-michael-harzenleiten.terroir: Gneiss and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of St. Michael (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-st-michael-kirchweg.name: Ried Kirchweg
at-st-michael-kirchweg.summary: A Ried along the old church path between Wösendorf and St. Michael, giving fresh, fruity Grüner Veltliner.
at-st-michael-kirchweg.terroir: Loess and sand. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of St. Michael (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-stein-hinters-kirchl.name: Ried Hinters Kirchl
at-stein-hinters-kirchl.summary: A small Stein Ried behind a chapel ('behind the little church'), giving fine Riesling and Grüner Veltliner; classified by the ÖTW.
at-stein-hinters-kirchl.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-stein-hinters-kirchl.terroir: Gneiss terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Stein (municipality Krems an der Donau).

at-stein-kogl.name: Ried Kögl
at-stein-kogl.summary: The Kögl is a high site above Krems where Salomon Undhof makes a delicate, peppery Grüner Veltliner.
at-stein-kogl.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-stein-kogl.terroir: Loess over gneiss. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Stein (municipality Krems an der Donau), with about 20 ha delimited.

at-stein-pfaffenberg.name: Ried Pfaffenberg
at-stein-pfaffenberg.summary: The Steiner Pfaffenberg is a steep, terraced slope west of Stein where the Wachau's crystalline rock continues into the Kremstal. Salomon Undhof's Riesling from here is one of Austria's classic dry whites: cool, floral and stony. The terraces climb steeply from Stein's old town and face Göttweig abbey across the Danube. The Salomon family has owned the Undhof since 1792.
at-stein-pfaffenberg.terroir: Gneiss and amphibolite terraces facing south over the Danube. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Stein (municipality Krems an der Donau), with about 30 ha delimited.
at-stein-pfaffenberg.nerd_note: 'Pfaffen' means priests, a pointer to former church ownership.

at-stein-steiner-goldberg.name: Ried Steiner Goldberg
at-stein-steiner-goldberg.summary: A Stein Ried giving fine Riesling on crystalline rock.
at-stein-steiner-goldberg.nerd_note: Kremstal DAC (since 2007) is reserved for Grüner Veltliner and Riesling; single-Ried wines form the top tier of its pyramid.
at-stein-steiner-goldberg.terroir: Gneiss terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Stein (municipality Krems an der Donau), with about 20 ha delimited.

at-stein-steiner-hund.name: Ried Steiner Hund
at-stein-steiner-hund.summary: The Steiner Hund is a small, steep slope above Stein whose Riesling, above all from Nikolaihof, is famously long-lived and mineral. Nikolaihof's Steiner Hund, from steep terraces above Stein, is one of Austria's longest-lived dry Rieslings, often still youthful at twenty; the estate has farmed biodynamically since 1971.
at-stein-steiner-hund.terroir: Gneiss terraces facing south. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Stein (municipality Krems an der Donau), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-stein-wachtberg.name: Ried Wachtberg
at-stein-wachtberg.summary: The Wachtberg rises above the old town of Krems, a terraced site that the Weingut Stadt Krems (owned by the town since the fifteenth century) has made its flagship. The Grüner Veltliner is dense and spicy, the Riesling fine and stony.
at-stein-wachtberg.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist terraces with loess pockets, facing south over the Krems valley. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Stein (municipality Krems an der Donau).
at-stein-wachtberg.nerd_note: Krems was a medieval wine-trading city; the town estate's vineyards include plots documented since the Middle Ages.

at-steinaweg-gottschelle.name: Ried Gottschelle
at-steinaweg-gottschelle.summary: The Gottschelle lies below Göttweig abbey on the south bank of the Danube, giving ripe, peppery Grüner Veltliner; Stift Göttweig's estate bottles it.
at-steinaweg-gottschelle.terroir: Loess over gravel and crystalline rock. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Steinaweg (municipality Furth bei Göttweig).

at-strass-gaisberg.name: Ried Gaisberg
at-strass-gaisberg.summary: The Strass side of the Gaisberg hill, giving fine, mineral Riesling and Grüner Veltliner; Straß growers sell it as Strasser Gaisberg.
at-strass-gaisberg.terroir: Gneiss and loess on the eastern slopes of the hill. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Straß (municipality Straß im Straßertale), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-strass-hasel.name: Ried Hasel
at-strass-hasel.summary: The Straß part of the Hasel Ried, giving fruity Grüner Veltliner on loess.
at-strass-hasel.nerd_note: Kamptal DAC (since 2008) puts Ried-designated Grüner Veltliner and Riesling at the top of its origin pyramid, above village and regional wines.
at-strass-hasel.terroir: Loess and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Straß (municipality Straß im Straßertale), with about 150 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Steinbühel.

at-strass-hasel-steinbuhel.name: Ried Hasel Steinbühel
at-strass-hasel-steinbuhel.summary: Steinbühel is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Hasel at Straß, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Straß part of the Hasel Ried, giving fruity Grüner Veltliner on loess.
at-strass-hasel-steinbuhel.nerd_note: See the Ried Hasel profile for the site's history and growers.

at-strass-offenberg.name: Ried Offenberg
at-strass-offenberg.summary: A small Straß Ried giving fresh, peppery Grüner Veltliner.
at-strass-offenberg.nerd_note: Kamptal DAC (since 2008) puts Ried-designated Grüner Veltliner and Riesling at the top of its origin pyramid, above village and regional wines.
at-strass-offenberg.terroir: Loess over rock. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Straß (municipality Straß im Straßertale), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-strass-wechselberg.name: Ried Wechselberg
at-strass-wechselberg.summary: The Wechselberg at Straß includes the subrieden Himmel and Spiegel, giving fine Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-strass-wechselberg.nerd_note: Kamptal DAC (since 2008) puts Ried-designated Grüner Veltliner and Riesling at the top of its origin pyramid, above village and regional wines.
at-strass-wechselberg.terroir: Gneiss and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Straß (municipality Straß im Straßertale), with about 30 ha delimited.

at-strass-wechselberg-himmel.name: Ried Wechselberg Himmel
at-strass-wechselberg-himmel.summary: Himmel is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Wechselberg at Straß, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Wechselberg at Straß includes the subrieden Himmel and Spiegel, giving fine Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-strass-wechselberg-himmel.nerd_note: See the Ried Wechselberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-strass-wechselberg-spiegel.name: Ried Wechselberg Spiegel
at-strass-wechselberg-spiegel.summary: Spiegel is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Wechselberg at Straß, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Wechselberg at Straß includes the subrieden Himmel and Spiegel, giving fine Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
at-strass-wechselberg-spiegel.nerd_note: See the Ried Wechselberg profile for the site's history and growers.

at-tattendorf-holzspur.name: Ried Holzspur
at-tattendorf-holzspur.summary: A Tattendorf Ried on stony gravel in the southern Thermenregion, known for Pinot Noir and St. Laurent from Johanneshof Reinisch.
at-tattendorf-holzspur.terroir: Calcareous gravel of the Steinfeld plain, warm and dry. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Tattendorf, with about 30 ha delimited.

at-tattendorf-steingarten.name: Ried Steingarten
at-tattendorf-steingarten.summary: A Tattendorf Ried of stony gravel giving firm St. Laurent and Pinot Noir.
at-tattendorf-steingarten.nerd_note: The Thermenregion, south of Vienna, is the home of Zierfandler and Rotgipfler on the limestone slopes near Gumpoldskirchen and of Pinot Noir and St. Laurent on the warm gravel plain around Tattendorf.
at-tattendorf-steingarten.terroir: Gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Tattendorf, with about 30 ha delimited.

at-thallern-frauengrund.name: Ried Frauengrund
at-thallern-frauengrund.summary: A Ried shared by Angern and Thallern in the Krems municipality, giving supple Grüner Veltliner.
at-thallern-frauengrund.terroir: Loess and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Thallern (municipality Krems an der Donau), with about 20 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Schweren Zapfen.

at-thallern-frauengrund-schweren-zapfen.name: Ried Frauengrund Schweren Zapfen
at-thallern-frauengrund-schweren-zapfen.summary: Schweren Zapfen is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Frauengrund at Thallern, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Ried shared by Angern and Thallern in the Krems municipality, giving supple Grüner Veltliner.
at-thallern-frauengrund-schweren-zapfen.nerd_note: See the Ried Frauengrund profile for the site's history and growers.

at-thurnthal-schafflerberg.name: Ried Schafflerberg
at-thurnthal-schafflerberg.summary: A Wagram Ried on the loess escarpment, giving fresh Grüner Veltliner and Roter Veltliner.
at-thurnthal-schafflerberg.nerd_note: The Wagram's loess bank runs for some 30 km along the north side of the Danube; its DAC rules put Ried wines at the top of the pyramid, with Grüner Veltliner and the local Roter Veltliner as signature grapes.
at-thurnthal-schafflerberg.terroir: Deep loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Thürnthal (municipality Fels am Wagram), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-traiskirchen-mandel-hoh.name: Ried Mandel-Höh
at-traiskirchen-mandel-hoh.summary: The Mandel-Höh above Traiskirchen is a limestone site classified by the ÖTW and the home of Stadlmann's celebrated Zierfandler, the rare local variety that, with Rotgipfler, defines the Thermenregion's white wines. Mandel-Höh Zierfandler is dense, spicy and famously long-lived, with orange peel and quince over a firm acidity that lets it age twenty years.
at-traiskirchen-mandel-hoh.terroir: Limestone and calcareous gravel on the edge of the Vienna Woods. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Traiskirchen.
at-traiskirchen-mandel-hoh.nerd_note: Zierfandler is also called Spätrot because its berries turn reddish late in the season.

at-traiskirchen-rodauner.name: Ried Rodauner
at-traiskirchen-rodauner.summary: A Traiskirchen Ried classified by the ÖTW, known for full, spicy Rotgipfler and Zierfandler from Alphart.
at-traiskirchen-rodauner.nerd_note: The Thermenregion, south of Vienna, is the home of Zierfandler and Rotgipfler on the limestone slopes near Gumpoldskirchen and of Pinot Noir and St. Laurent on the warm gravel plain around Tattendorf.
at-traiskirchen-rodauner.terroir: Calcareous gravel and loam; with the subried Otzler. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Traiskirchen, with about 10 ha delimited.

at-traiskirchen-rodauner-otzler.name: Ried Rodauner Otzler
at-traiskirchen-rodauner-otzler.summary: Otzler is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Rodauner at Traiskirchen, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Traiskirchen Ried classified by the ÖTW, known for full, spicy Rotgipfler and Zierfandler from Alphart.
at-traiskirchen-rodauner-otzler.terroir: Calcareous gravel and loam; with the subried Otzler.
at-traiskirchen-rodauner-otzler.nerd_note: See the Ried Rodauner profile for the site's history and growers.
at-traiskirchen-rodauner-otzler.classification: ÖTW Erste Lage (1ÖTW) (as part of the Ried Rodauner)

at-traismauer-brunnberg.name: Ried Brunnberg
at-traismauer-brunnberg.summary: A Traismauer Ried at the northern end of the valley, giving fruity white wines.
at-traismauer-brunnberg.nerd_note: Traisental DAC (since 2006) covers Grüner Veltliner and Riesling from one of the smallest wine areas of Lower Austria, on the south side of the Danube.
at-traismauer-brunnberg.terroir: Loess and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Traismauer, with about 30 ha delimited.

at-unterloiben-burgstall.name: Ried Burgstall
at-unterloiben-burgstall.summary: A Loiben Ried on gentle slopes, giving fresh Grüner Veltliner.
at-unterloiben-burgstall.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
at-unterloiben-burgstall.terroir: Loess and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Unterloiben (municipality Dürnstein), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-unterloiben-frauenweingarten.name: Ried Frauenweingarten
at-unterloiben-frauenweingarten.summary: The 'ladies' vineyard' at Loiben recalls the convent of Dürnstein; it gives round, fruity Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.

at-unterloiben-kreutles.name: Ried Kreutles
at-unterloiben-kreutles.summary: A flatter Loiben site of loess and alluvium where Knoll and others make juicy, peppery Grüner Veltliner.
at-unterloiben-kreutles.terroir: Deep loess and sand near the Danube. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Unterloiben (municipality Dürnstein), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-unterloiben-loibenberg.name: Ried Loibenberg
at-unterloiben-loibenberg.summary: The Loibenberg is the great sun-trap of Loiben, a broad, steep amphitheatre of terraces above Unterloiben facing full south. Its wines are ripe, rich and spicy, with Riesling showing apricot and Grüner Veltliner tobacco and pepper. Knoll, F.X. Pichler, Leo Alzinger and Tegernseerhof are reference growers. Some growers now worry that in hot summers it can become too warm, which is why cooler sites are gaining favour.
at-unterloiben-loibenberg.terroir: About 40 ha registered, gneiss and paragneiss with loess on the lower parts; subrieden include Süssenberg, Rothenberg, Langen Zung and Rauheneck. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Unterloiben (municipality Dürnstein), with about 40 ha delimited.
at-unterloiben-loibenberg.nerd_note: The Loibenberg is the Wachau's warmest large site because the valley opens towards the Pannonian east here.

at-unterloiben-muhlpoint.summary: A Loiben site on lower ground where Leo Alzinger makes a fresh, peppery Grüner Veltliner.

at-unterloiben-schutt.name: Ried Schütt
at-unterloiben-schutt.summary: The Schütt is a site of alluvial gravel and sand washed down from a side valley between Dürnstein and Loiben. Knoll's Riesling Smaragd Schütt is one of the Wachau's classics, broad and juicy with a peppery bite.
at-unterloiben-schutt.terroir: Gravel, sand and gneiss debris on a gentle fan at the foot of the hills. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Unterloiben (municipality Dürnstein).
at-unterloiben-schutt.nerd_note: 'Schütt' means debris or rubble, describing the material the side valley dumps onto the slope.

at-unterloiben-steinertal.name: Ried Steinertal
at-unterloiben-steinertal.summary: The Steinertal is a narrow, steep side valley above Loiben where cool air drains down at night. Its Rieslings, especially from Leo Alzinger and F.X. Pichler, are among the most delicate and crystalline of the Wachau. Cool air drains down the valley from the Waldviertel plateau at night, so night temperatures are lower here than on the Loibenberg next door, and Alzinger's Steinertal Riesling is often the most perfumed wine of the estate.
at-unterloiben-steinertal.terroir: Gneiss terraces in a cool, north-south side valley. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Unterloiben (municipality Dürnstein), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-viessling-bruck.name: Ried Bruck
at-viessling-bruck.summary: The Bruck in the Spitzer Graben is one of the side valley's best-known Rieden, giving delicate, high-toned Riesling. Several terraces here were rescued from abandonment by a new generation of growers after 2000. Peter Veyder-Malberg came to the Spitzer Graben in 2008 and rescued abandoned terraces that larger estates had given up as uneconomic.
at-viessling-bruck.terroir: Steep gneiss terraces in a cool side valley. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Vießling (municipality Spitz), with about 20 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Stern.

at-viessling-bruck-stern.name: Ried Bruck Stern
at-viessling-bruck-stern.summary: Stern is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Bruck at Vießling, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. at-viessling-schon.name: Ried Schön
at-viessling-schon.summary: A Ried in the Spitzer Graben, the cool side valley behind Spitz where terraces climb to over 500 m. Growers such as Peter Veyder-Malberg, Martin Muthenthaler and Johann Donabaum make lean, ethereal Riesling and Grüner Veltliner here, a different face of the Wachau from the warm river sites.
at-viessling-schon.terroir: Gneiss and amphibolite terraces in a narrow, cool valley. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Vießling (municipality Spitz), with about 10 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Hölle.

at-weissenkirchen-achleiten.name: Ried Achleiten
at-weissenkirchen-achleiten.summary: The Achleiten is the great hill of Weißenkirchen and Joching, a bulging promontory of terraces that rises from the Danube at the downstream end of the village. It is one of the most complex sites of the Wachau, and its Rieslings and Grüner Veltliners combine ripe stone fruit with a smoky, salty, almost flinty minerality that tasters recognise blind. Prager (where Toni Bodenstein studied the site's geology in detail), Domäne Wachau, Rudi Pichler and Holzapfel make reference Smaragd wines.
at-weissenkirchen-achleiten.terroir: About 22 ha of dry-stone terraces between roughly 200 and 360 m, facing south and south-west. The lower slope is mica schist and paragneiss; higher up come gneiss and dark amphibolite, with patches of loess and marble (metamorphosed limestone). Topsoil is thin, so the vines root into the rock. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Weißenkirchen (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 20 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Himmelreich.
at-weissenkirchen-achleiten.nerd_note: Bodenstein has pointed to bands of amphibolite and serpentinite running through the hill and links these magnesium-rich rocks to the wines' salty edge; the subried Achleiten Himmelreich is the uppermost part.

at-weissenkirchen-achleiten-himmelreich.summary: Himmelreich is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Achleiten at Weißenkirchen, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. at-weissenkirchen-achleiten-himmelreich.nerd_note: Himmelreich ('kingdom of heaven') is the uppermost part of the Achleiten, where gneiss dominates and the wines are at their most taut.

at-weissenkirchen-buschenberg.name: Ried Buschenberg
at-weissenkirchen-buschenberg.summary: A Weißenkirchen Ried giving fine, mineral Riesling and Grüner Veltliner from terraces above the village.

at-weissenkirchen-hinter-der-burg.name: Ried Hinter der Burg
at-weissenkirchen-hinter-der-burg.summary: Hinter der Burg ('behind the castle') is a Weißenkirchen site best known for Prager's crisp Grüner Veltliner Federspiel.
at-weissenkirchen-hinter-der-burg.terroir: Loess and gneiss on lower terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Weißenkirchen (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 10 ha delimited.

at-weissenkirchen-klaus.name: Ried Klaus
at-weissenkirchen-klaus.summary: The Klaus is a steep, narrow terraced site between Weißenkirchen and Joching that Josef Jamek made famous: his Riesling Ried Klaus of the late 1950s is often cited as the first great dry single-vineyard Riesling of the Wachau, at a time when most Austrian wine was sweetened. Today Prager, Jamek and others make taut, mineral Riesling here. The narrow terraces are among the steepest of Weißenkirchen and can only be worked by hand.
at-weissenkirchen-klaus.terroir: About 15 to 20 ha of gneiss and amphibolite terraces facing south-east, sheltered by the Achleiten hill. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Weißenkirchen (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 20 ha delimited.
at-weissenkirchen-klaus.nerd_note: Jamek's family inn in Joching, run for more than a century, was where many visitors first tasted dry Wachau Riesling.

at-weissenkirchen-ritzling.name: Ried Ritzling

at-weissenkirchen-seiberberg.name: Ried Seiberberg
at-weissenkirchen-seiberberg.summary: The Seiberberg rises high behind Weißenkirchen, a cool site whose Riesling and Grüner Veltliner are taut and perfumed.
at-weissenkirchen-seiberberg.terroir: Gneiss terraces at around 400 m, among the higher Wachau sites. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Weißenkirchen (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 30 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Hochseiber.

at-weissenkirchen-steinriegl.name: Ried Steinriegl
at-weissenkirchen-steinriegl.summary: The Steinriegl ('stone ridge') climbs high behind Weißenkirchen, one of the coolest top sites of the village thanks to its altitude and the winds that drop out of the Waldviertel forest at night. Prager and Domäne Wachau make sleek, perfumed Riesling here.
at-weissenkirchen-steinriegl.terroir: Terraces of gneiss and mica schist rising to over 400 m, south-facing; cooler nights than the river-side sites. at-weissenkirchen-vorderseiber.name: Ried Vorderseiber
at-weissenkirchen-vorderseiber.summary: The Vorderseiber is the lower, warmer part of the Seiber hill behind Weißenkirchen, giving full Grüner Veltliner on loess-rich terraces.

at-weissenkirchen-zwerithaler.summary: A tiny, steep Weißenkirchen Ried where Prager makes a fine, cool Riesling Smaragd.

at-winden-am-see-kirchberg.summary: A Winden Ried on the northern Leitha hills, giving Blaufränkisch and Chardonnay from schist and limestone.
at-winden-am-see-kirchberg.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
at-winden-am-see-kirchberg.terroir: Schist and limestone. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Winden am See, with about 130 ha delimited.

at-wosendorf-hochrain.name: Ried Hochrain
at-wosendorf-hochrain.summary: The Hochrain above Wösendorf gives some of the Wachau's most elegant Grüner Veltliner and Riesling, notably from Rudi Pichler and Franz Hirtzberger. Loess on the lower terraces softens the wines, gneiss above sharpens them. Rudi Pichler, whose winery stands in Wösendorf, ferments with natural yeasts and gives his wines long lees contact; his Hochrain Grüner Veltliner Smaragd is one of the region's most age-worthy.

at-wosendorf-kollmitz.summary: A small Ried between Joching and Wösendorf, giving fine, aromatic Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.

at-wosendorf-kollmutz.summary: The Kollmütz behind Wösendorf is known above all for Rudi Pichler's Grüner Veltliner Smaragd, a dense, peppery wine from loess-rich terraces.

at-zobing-gaisberg.name: Ried Gaisberg
at-zobing-gaisberg.summary: The Gaisberg is the Heiligenstein's neighbour to the east, but its rock is different: crystalline gneiss, amphibolite and mica schist rather than sandstone. The result is a cooler, more floral and filigree Riesling, with white flowers and citrus, that many tasters prefer for its finesse. Hirsch, Bründlmayer and Schloss Gobelsburg are the leading growers.
at-zobing-gaisberg.terroir: Terraces of gneiss and mica schist with thin soils, facing south and south-east, rising to over 300 m; the hill spans Zöbing and Kammern. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Zöbing (municipality Langenlois), with about 30 ha delimited.
at-zobing-gaisberg.nerd_note: Johannes Hirsch, one of the first Austrian estates to move to screwcaps for top wines in 2002, made his name with Gaisberg and Heiligenstein Rieslings.

at-zobing-heiligenstein.name: Ried Heiligenstein
at-zobing-heiligenstein.summary: The Heiligenstein is the Kamptal's most famous hill and one of the great Riesling sites of Austria, a south-facing ridge above Zöbing; local tradition holds that its name ('holy stone') is a pious rewriting of an older 'Höllenstein', hell's stone, a nod to its summer heat. It is geologically unique in the region: instead of gneiss or loess, it is built of Permian desert sandstone and conglomerate with volcanic components, about 270 million years old, the so-called Zöbing formation. Its Rieslings are spicy, smoky and long, with a citrus and stone-fruit core and a firm, salty finish. More than a dozen owners share it, led by Bründlmayer, Hirsch, Schloss Gobelsburg, Jurtschitsch, Allram and Hiedler.
at-zobing-heiligenstein.terroir: About 35 ha of terraces between roughly 240 and 350 m. The sandstone weathers into a poor, brittle, stony soil; cool north winds from the Waldviertel ventilate the hill and keep acidity high, while the south face gets intense sun. Subrieden on the official map include Heiligenstein-Rotfels and Heiligenstein-Steinwand. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Zöbing (municipality Langenlois), with about 40 ha delimited.
at-zobing-heiligenstein.nerd_note: Bründlmayer pioneered the open 'lyre' trellis here in the 1980s to spread the canopy and ripen grapes evenly on this exposed hill.

at-zobing-kogelberg.name: Ried Kogelberg
at-zobing-kogelberg.summary: A Ried on the hills west of Langenlois, giving fresh Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
at-zobing-kogelberg.nerd_note: Kamptal DAC (since 2008) puts Ried-designated Grüner Veltliner and Riesling at the top of its origin pyramid, above village and regional wines.
at-zobing-kogelberg.terroir: Gneiss and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Zöbing (municipality Langenlois), with about 80 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Eichelberg, Wechselberg.
